zh_alt: 示意圖，分成四段，講四套超音波風險分層表對同一顆甲狀腺結節不會給同一個答案。第一段把四套表並排：ACR TI-RADS（美國放射學會的白皮書）、美國甲狀腺學會 2015 年版的五型態表、歐洲的 EU-TIRADS、韓國的 K-TIRADS。每一欄畫兩條比例條，數字來自同一篇納入 11 篇原著、對象是 1 公分以上結節的統合分析，括號裡是 95% 信賴區間。圖上標明「不必要切片率」的分母不是所有被掃到的人，而是這套表建議去扎的那些結節，分子是其中最後證實為良性的那些。不必要切片率：ACR TI-RADS 41%（32–49）、美國甲狀腺學會 2015 年版 65%（56–74）、EU-TIRADS 68%（60–75）、2016 年版 K-TIRADS 79%（74–83）；敏感度的排序幾乎是倒過來的：2016 年版 K-TIRADS 96%（94–97）、美國甲狀腺學會 2015 年版 89%（85–93）、EU-TIRADS 88%（81–92）、ACR TI-RADS 82%（74–87）。K-TIRADS 那一欄另外註明，2021 年版改用 1.5 公分切點之後，不必要切片率降到 50%（47–53）、敏感度跟著掉到 76%（74–79），而且現行版是 2021 年版不是 2016 年版；那一欄的切點來自 225 顆結節的比較研究，和 2021 年韓國那份共識列的一樣。每一欄下面列出自己的扎針切點：ACR TI-RADS 第 3 級 2.5 公分以上、第 4 級 1.5 公分以上、第 5 級 1 公分以上，計分制裡第 3 級是 3 分、第 4 級 4 到 6 分、第 5 級 7 分以上，而且邊緣鈣化這個特徵只有這一套給分；美國甲狀腺學會 2015 年版的第 8 條建議是高度可疑 1 公分以上扎（強烈建議、中等品質證據）、中度可疑 1 公分以上扎（強烈建議、低品質證據）、低度可疑要 1.5 公分以上才扎而且只是弱建議、極低度可疑要 2 公分以上才「考慮」扎、純囊狀不必切片（強烈建議），同一份文件配的風險估計是高度可疑 70% 到 90% 以上、中度可疑 10% 到 20%、低度可疑 5% 到 10%、極低度可疑低於 3%、純囊狀低於 1%；EU-TIRADS 第 3 類 20 毫米以上、第 4 類 15 毫米以上、第 5 類 10 毫米以上；K-TIRADS 第 3 類 2 公分以上、第 4 類 1 到 1.5 公分之間、第 5 類 1 公分以上。圖上同時標明：ACR 的白皮書原文與歐洲那份原始指引這次都取不到全文，分級與切點是轉引自那篇把三套表逐欄列出來的比較研究，不是從原始文件抄的；美國甲狀腺學會 2025 年的新版把甲狀腺結節整塊拿掉了，結節這一塊沒有新版，所以那一欄講的是 2015 年版而不是最新版。這一段旁邊有一個灰底說明：另一篇納入 67 篇、76,512 顆結節的統合分析比的是分類切點而不是扎針建議，排出來的順序就不一樣，兩篇的問題不同，答案自然不同，所以這張圖不排名次。第二段是三條橫條，比的是同一批結節裡三套表各自漏掉幾顆惡性。族群是一項單中心的前瞻性研究，225 顆結節，其中 23.1% 最後證實是惡性，三套表同時跑一遍；ACR TI-RADS 漏 11 顆惡性、EU-TIRADS 漏 5 顆、K-TIRADS 漏 3 顆。下面一行寫漏掉的典型長相是同一種：直徑 1.0 到 1.5 公分之間的實質高回音結節；反過來也有，邊緣鈣化這個特徵只有 ACR TI-RADS 給分，另外兩套根本不計。第三段是那一顆結節的實例，三格並排，同一顆結節、同一天、同一張超音波影像：ACR TI-RADS 給第 3 級（只拿到 3 分），扎針切點是 2.5 公分以上，結論是不扎；EU-TIRADS 給第 5 類，切點 1.0 公分以上，結論是扎；K-TIRADS 給第 4 類，切點 1.0 公分以上，結論是扎。這一段下面有一個黃底說明，交代 K-TIRADS 第 4 類那一格寫的是一個區間不是一個數字：同一篇比較研究的表格把切點寫成 1 到 1.5 公分之間，因為那一格本來就是一個區間——切點要在 1 到 1.5 公分之間，依超音波特徵、結節位置與臨床因素決定，所以這一顆 1.0 到 1.5 公分的結節落在區間的下緣、用的是 1.0 公分；這三個切點和 2021 年韓國那份共識列的一樣。第四段講同一套表在大結節和小結節上表現也不一樣，族群是 3,826 顆 1 公分以上的結節，其中 85.7% 良性、14.3% 惡性：2 公分以下的結節，ACR TI-RADS 省下的不必要切片最多，76.3%，但它的敏感度也是五套裡最低的，76.1%；2 公分以上的結節，ACR TI-RADS 的敏感度是 88.8%，明顯低於其他系統的 98.7% 到 99.3%。這一段的結語是：你的結節被哪一套表看、又剛好是多大，這兩件事合起來會決定你今天要不要挨那一針，這不是一句抱怨，這是現況。圖的最後是一個紅框的界線區塊，標題是「這張圖不是用來替你那一顆打分數的」，內容有四條：圖上沒有任何一欄可以讓你替自己算分數，分數來自超音波影像上的形狀特徵，那是判讀的人在機器前面做的事；不必要切片率與敏感度是同一個天平的兩端，抓得多就扎得多、扎得少就會漏，所以「哪一套最準」這個問題沒有答案，圖上也不替讀者選一套；ACR 白皮書與歐洲原始指引都取不到全文，圖上的分級與切點是轉引；讀者能做的是把它問出口——我這份報告用的是哪一套分類、報告上有寫分級嗎、照這套表決定的是大小還是形狀、換另一套表來看答案會不會不一樣。
en_alt: Schematic in four parts, showing that four ultrasound risk-stratification systems do not give the same answer about the same thyroid nodule. The first part sets the four tables side by side: ACR TI-RADS (American College of Radiology, white paper), the five sonographic patterns of the 2015 American Thyroid Association guidelines, the European EU-TIRADS, and the Korean K-TIRADS. Each column carries two proportional bars whose figures come from one meta-analysis of 11 primary studies of nodules 1 cm and larger, with 95% confidence intervals in brackets. The figure states that the denominator of the unnecessary-biopsy rate is not everyone scanned but the nodules the table recommends biopsying, and the numerator is those of them that turned out benign. Unnecessary biopsy rate: ACR TI-RADS 41% (32-49), ATA 2015 65% (56-74), EU-TIRADS 68% (60-75), K-TIRADS 2016 edition 79% (74-83). The sensitivities run almost in the reverse order: K-TIRADS 2016 edition 96% (94-97), ATA 2015 89% (85-93), EU-TIRADS 88% (81-92), ACR TI-RADS 82% (74-87). The K-TIRADS column adds that once the 2021 edition moved to a 1.5 cm cutoff the unnecessary biopsy rate fell to 50% (47-53) and the sensitivity fell with it to 76% (74-79), and that the current edition is 2021, not 2016; that column's cutoffs come from the 225-nodule comparison study and are the same ones listed in the 2021 Korean consensus. Each column lists its own biopsy cutoffs. ACR TI-RADS: TR3 at 2.5 cm and above, TR4 at 1.5 cm and above, TR5 at 1 cm and above, where TR3 is 3 points, TR4 is 4 to 6 points and TR5 is 7 or more, and rim calcification is scored by this table alone. ATA 2015, Recommendation 8: high suspicion biopsied at 1 cm and above (strong recommendation, moderate-quality evidence), intermediate suspicion at 1 cm and above (strong recommendation, low-quality evidence), low suspicion only at 1.5 cm and above and only as a weak recommendation, very low suspicion merely "considered" at 2 cm and above, and purely cystic nodules not biopsied (strong recommendation); the risk estimates in the same document are 70% to over 90% for high suspicion, 10% to 20% for intermediate, 5% to 10% for low, under 3% for very low and under 1% for purely cystic. EU-TIRADS: category 3 at 20 mm and above, category 4 at 15 mm and above, category 5 at 10 mm and above. K-TIRADS: category 3 at 2 cm and above, category 4 between 1 and 1.5 cm, category 5 at 1 cm and above. The figure states on its face that neither the ACR white paper nor the original European guideline could be obtained in full, so the categories and cutoffs shown are carried over from the comparison study that lists all three tables column by column rather than copied from the primary documents; and that the 2025 edition from the American Thyroid Association dropped thyroid nodules altogether, with no newer nodule document published, so that column is the 2015 edition and not the latest. A grey note beside this part explains that a second meta-analysis, of 67 studies and 76,512 nodules, compares classification cutoffs rather than biopsy recommendations and therefore ranks the systems differently; the two ask different questions, so the figure declines to rank them. The second part is three horizontal bars comparing how many cancers each table missed in the same series. The cohort is a single-centre prospective study of 225 nodules, of which 23.1% proved malignant, with three tables run over all of them: ACR TI-RADS missed 11 malignancies, EU-TIRADS missed 5, K-TIRADS missed 3. A line underneath records that the misses share one appearance, a solid hyperechoic nodule between 1.0 and 1.5 cm across, and that it runs the other way too, since rim calcification is scored by ACR TI-RADS alone. The third part is that nodule as a worked case, in three panels, for one nodule on one day on one ultrasound image: ACR TI-RADS calls it TR3 with only 3 points, where the biopsy cutoff is 2.5 cm and above, so it is not biopsied; EU-TIRADS calls it category 5, cutoff 1.0 cm and above, so it is biopsied; K-TIRADS calls it category 4, cutoff 1.0 cm and above, so it is biopsied. A yellow note below explains that the K-TIRADS category 4 cell holds a range rather than a single number: the table in that comparison study gives the cutoff as between 1 and 1.5 cm because that cell is a range in the first place, the cutoff being set between 1 and 1.5 cm according to the ultrasound features, the position of the nodule and clinical factors, so this nodule of 1.0 to 1.5 cm sits at the bottom of the range, at 1.0 cm; these three cutoffs are the same ones listed in the 2021 Korean consensus. The fourth part shows that one table performs differently on large and small nodules, in a series of 3,826 nodules 1 cm and larger of which 85.7% were benign and 14.3% malignant: below 2 cm, ACR TI-RADS spares the most unnecessary biopsies at 76.3% and has the lowest sensitivity of the five at 76.1%; above 2 cm, ACR TI-RADS reaches a sensitivity of 88.8%, clearly below the 98.7% to 99.3% of the other systems. The closing line of that part is that which table happened to read your nodule, and how large that nodule happens to be, together decide whether you are biopsied today; this is not a complaint but the present state of things. The figure ends with a red-bordered block headed "This figure will not score your nodule", holding four statements: no column here lets a reader work out their own points, because the score comes from shape features on the image judged by the person at the machine; unnecessary-biopsy rate and sensitivity are two ends of one set of scales, so catching more means biopsying more and biopsying less means missing more, and the question of which table is most accurate has no answer, with no system chosen for the reader; the ACR white paper and the original European guideline could not be obtained in full, so the categories and cutoffs shown are carried over from the comparison study; and what a reader can do is ask out loud which system their report uses, whether the report states a category, whether the decision under that system is being made by size or by shape, and whether another table would give a different answer.

zh_alt: 示意圖，把 2023 年第三版甲狀腺細胞病理報告系統的六個類別、各自的惡性機率與各自的下一步排成六列。每一列左邊是類別編號與第三版的英文名稱，中間是惡性機率的平均值、括號裡的範圍與一條比例條，右邊是這一類接下來會走的路。這一組數字有四個標籤要一起帶：第三版、成人、給的是平均值與括號裡的範圍、終點是「切除後組織病理確認為惡性」。六列由第一類排到第六類，每一列的比例條用同一把 0 到 100 的尺畫，顏色隨機率由淺到深，從第一列的中性色、經過綠與金，到最後兩列的紅。第一類 nondiagnostic（不足以判讀）13%（5–20），下一步是在超音波導引下重扎；圖上註明第一類不是「沒事」，是「這次沒抽到東西」。第二類 benign（良性）4%（2–7），下一步是臨床與超音波追蹤。第三類 atypia of undetermined significance（意義未明的非典型）22%（13–30），下一步是重扎、分子檢測、診斷性單葉切除或監測。第四類 follicular neoplasm（濾泡性腫瘤）30%（23–34），下一步是分子檢測或診斷性單葉切除。第五類 suspicious for malignancy（疑似惡性）74%（67–83），下一步是進到手術的討論。第六類 malignant（惡性）97%（97–100），下一步同樣是進到手術的討論。第二段處理第三類裡面的兩格：第三版把第三類拆成兩個次分類，AUS-nuclear（細胞核有非典型變化）在切除檢體上是 36% 到 44%，AUS-other（其他型態的非典型）是 15% 到 23%。旁邊的黃底說明寫另一篇回顧把「其他型態」再拆得更細：細胞核非典型 36% 到 48%、結構非典型 10% 到 20%、嗜酸性細胞型 5% 到 6%；所以當報告寫第三類，值得問的下一個問題是「是哪一種第三類」，這一句問下去，22% 可能會變成 15%，也可能會變成 44%。第三段是三件會讓新舊報告對不起來的事。第一件是名字換了，不代表當年那張報告判錯：AUS／FLUS 現在只叫 AUS；FN／SFN 現在只叫 FN，「疑似濾泡性腫瘤」這個詞已經被拿掉了；unsatisfactory 現在叫 nondiagnostic。第二件是 NIFTP 改判之後每一類的百分比都往下掉了：第三版把一種叫 NIFTP 的腫瘤改判為非癌以後，各類的惡性機率都往下掉了 1.3% 到 9.1%，所以拿舊報告的百分比去對新報告會對錯。第三件是第一類與第三類各自有一條品管線：夠不夠判讀有客觀標準，至少六群保存良好的濾泡細胞、每一群至少十個細胞，出現在一張或多張玻片上，沒有達到就落到第一類；第三類的判讀最好不要超過全部細針檢體的 7% 到 10%，而第三類對第六類的比值最好在 3 以下，這一類被用得太浮濫本身就是品質問題。圖上沒有任何一格把編號直接換成一個決定：每一列的機率旁邊都配著它自己的下一步，最低的兩類走的是再取一次檢體或追蹤，最高的兩類走的是「進到手術的討論」，而不是手術本身。圖的最後是一個紅框的界線區塊，標題是「這張圖不是你的機率」，內容有四條：這六個數字是平均值，分母是一整批被切除並做了組織病理的檢體，不是你那一管，第三類寫 22% 不代表你有 22% 的機會是癌；這個編號跟期別無關，也不是「第幾期」，它是細胞學的分類，回答的只有「這一管細胞有多大機會是惡性」這一個問題；這些機率與下一步都是轉引，兩篇文獻的表格都註明是經授權改編自第三版原書，這次沒有拿到原書；拿到編號之後可以照著念的是——我這張報告是第幾類？如果是第三類，是細胞核那一種還是其他那一種？這份報告用的是第幾版的分類？
en_alt: Schematic setting out the six categories of the 2023 third edition of the Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology as six rows, each with its risk of malignancy and its next step. Each row carries the category number and the third edition's English name on the left, the average risk of malignancy with its expected range and a proportional bar in the middle, and the road that category leads to on the right. Four labels travel with the figures: third edition, adults, average with the expected range in brackets, and the endpoint is malignancy confirmed on histology after resection. The six rows run in order from category I to category VI, each bar drawn to the same scale from zero to a hundred, and the colour deepens as the risk rises, from the neutral tone of the first row through teal and gold to the red of the last two. Category I, nondiagnostic, 13% (5-20), leading to a repeat FNA with ultrasound guidance; the figure notes that category I does not mean nothing is wrong, but that nothing was obtained this time. Category II, benign, 4% (2-7), leading to clinical and sonographic follow-up. Category III, atypia of undetermined significance, 22% (13-30), leading to a repeat FNA, molecular testing, diagnostic lobectomy, or surveillance. Category IV, follicular neoplasm, 30% (23-34), leading to molecular testing or diagnostic lobectomy. Category V, suspicious for malignancy, 74% (67-83), leading into the discussion about surgery. Category VI, malignant, 97% (97-100), leading into the same discussion. The second part opens category III, which the third edition split into two subcategories: AUS-nuclear, atypia of the nuclei, at 36% to 44% on resected specimens, and AUS-other, atypia of other kinds, at 15% to 23%. A note beside them records that a second review splits "other" more finely still, with nuclear atypia 36% to 48%, architectural atypia 10% to 20% and oncocytic 5% to 6%, and that when a report says category III the next question worth asking is which kind of category III, since asking it can turn 22% into 15% or into 44%. The third part lists three things that make an old report and a new one disagree. First, the names changed, which does not mean the old report was read wrongly: AUS/FLUS is now simply AUS; FN/SFN is now simply FN, and "suspicious for a follicular neoplasm" has been removed; unsatisfactory is now nondiagnostic. Second, after a tumour called NIFTP was reclassified as not cancer, the risk of malignancy fell in every category by 1.3% to 9.1%, so reading the percentages of an older report against a newer one gives the wrong answer. Third, categories I and III each carry a quality line: adequacy has an objective standard of at least six groups of well-visualised follicular cells, each of at least ten cells, on one or more slides, and anything short of that falls into category I; while category III should not exceed roughly 7% to 10% of all fine-needle specimens and the ratio of category III to category VI should stay under 3, because a category used too freely is itself a quality problem. Nothing in the figure turns a category into a decision on its own: each row pairs its risk with the step it leads to, and the two lowest categories lead to another sample or to follow-up rather than to an operation, while the two highest lead into a conversation about surgery rather than to surgery itself. The figure ends with a red-bordered block headed "These are not your odds", holding four statements: the six figures are averages whose denominator is a whole series of specimens that went on to resection and histology, not the reader's own sample, so a category III reading 22% does not mean a 22% chance of cancer; the number has nothing to do with stage and is not an answer to "what stage am I", being a cytology category that answers only how likely this sample is to be malignant; the risks and next steps are carried over, because both papers state that their tables are adapted with permission from the third-edition book, which was not obtained; and what a reader can say out loud once they have the number is which category the report is, whether a category III is the nuclear kind or the other kind, and which edition of the classification the report uses.

zh_alt: 示意圖，把甲狀腺癌報告上的兩個標籤畫成兩條分開的軸，中間用一條虛線隔開，而且刻意不畫任何箭頭連起來。圖首先寫明：兩套系統是為了不同的主要問題而建的，而不對稱只成立在一個方向——分期是為死亡建的，指引自己說它不足以預測復發，這正是當年另外做一套復發分層的理由。左邊是軸一，AJCC／TNM 期別，它預測的是死於這個病，也就是疾病特異性存活。這一欄引 2025 年美國甲狀腺學會分化型甲狀腺癌指引的原話：AJCC 與 UICC 的分期是為了預測疾病特異性存活而設計的，因此它不預測結構性殘存或復發的整體風險。接著是年齡切點：AJCC 第八版從 2018 年起生效，把分期用的年齡切點從 45 歲提高到 55 歲；美國甲狀腺學會 2015 年那一版指引的分期表用的還是第七版、切點寫 45 歲，2025 年版才是這個學會第一份以第八版為基礎的分化型甲狀腺癌指引；拿 2018 年以前的資料去對現在的報告會對錯。紅框那一格是第八版最常被誤讀的一句：所有 55 歲以下的病人都是第一期，除非有遠端轉移，那樣是第二期；反過來讀，一個 55 歲以下的人如果拿到「第二期」，依定義那代表已經有遠端轉移，「第二期而已」這四個字完全不成立。再下面是 55 歲以上的排法：腫瘤侷限在甲狀腺內、沒有轉移是第一期；加上淋巴結轉移，或腫瘤大於 4 公分、或肉眼侵犯帶狀肌，是第二期；肉眼侵犯到皮下軟組織、喉、氣管、食道或喉返神經是第三期；侵犯椎前筋膜或包覆頸動脈是第四期 A；有遠端轉移是第四期 B。旁註寫第八版另外兩項改動：只在顯微鏡下看到的甲狀腺外侵犯不再算進 T3 的定義，淋巴結轉移不再自動把人推到第三期。接著是版本位移：一篇納入 6 篇研究、10,850 名分化型甲狀腺癌病人、中位追蹤 55 到 148 個月的統合分析，把同一批人用兩個版本各排一次，畫成兩條堆疊條並列出四行數字：第一期 60% 變成 81%、第二期 5% 變成 13%、第三期 21% 變成 2%、第四期 10% 變成 3%。同一篇的 10 年疾病特異性存活按版本分列：第二期在第七版是 98.1%（96.6–99.6）、在第八版是 88.6%（82.7–94.6）；第三期在第七版是 96.8%（94.1–99.64）、在第八版是 70.5%（59.1–83.9）。說明寫：數字掉了快十個百分點，不是因為病人變差了，是因為裝進「第二期」這個盒子裡的人換了一批——指引的說法是有 20% 到 30% 的病人相較第七版降期，所以同樣寫著「第二期」的兩份報告，如果版本不同，指的其實不是同一種處境。右邊是軸二，ATA 復發風險分層，四級，它預測的是結構性疾病殘存或復發（局部區域和／或遠端），和／或存活。這一欄引 2015 年版的理由：因為 AJCC 與 TNM 這套為死亡風險設計的分期系統無法充分預測分化型甲狀腺癌的復發風險，所以 2009 年那一版指引才另外提出一套復發風險分層。四級用復發機率直接定義，畫成四格階梯：低是低於 10%、低—中間是 10% 到 15%、中間—高是 16% 到 30%、高是超過 30%。說明寫 2015 年版是三級（低、中、高），2025 年版變成四級，分家的理由指引自己有寫：原本「中」那一格裡的各個條件並不是每一個都預測同樣的復發風險；「低—中間」與「中間—高」這兩個中文名字是這個專題固定的譯法。下面一格寫 2025 年版第 28A 條被要求判定什麼，逐字是：判定結構性疾病殘存或復發（局部區域和／或遠端）和／或存活的風險，強烈建議、中等確定性證據；註記寫「和／或存活」常在轉述時被省掉但它在原文裡，所以復發風險分層的主要工作是結構性復發，而指引自己的條文又把它延伸到存活，反方向的那一句——復發分層不能預測死亡——指引沒有寫過。這一欄最後有一格黃底的老實交代：2025 年四級系統每一格的完整納入條件這次沒有取得，它在指引裡是一張圖、可擷取的文字只有四個級距的百分比，所以「什麼條件會被歸到哪一格」只能引 2015 年版那一張表——低風險要求沒有侵襲性亞型、沒有血管侵犯、沒有臨床上的淋巴結轉移；中風險包含顯微鏡下侵犯甲狀腺周圍軟組織、侵襲性亞型、乳突癌合併血管侵犯、臨床上可見的淋巴結轉移；高風險包含肉眼可見的甲狀腺外侵犯、切除不完全、遠端轉移、3 公分以上的轉移淋巴結，以及廣泛血管侵犯的濾泡癌。兩欄之間的虛線標著「兩條軸之間：沒有箭頭」。兩欄下面是一個打叉的方框，標題「這裡沒有箭頭」，旁邊寫：兩個標籤不能互相翻譯，「第一期」不等於「低風險」，「中間—高風險」也不是「第三期」，期別不是一個復發機率，風險組也不是一個死亡機率；不對稱只成立在一個方向——分期是為死亡建的，指引自己說它不足以預測復發，這正是另外做一套復發分層的理由，而復發分層的主要工作是結構性復發，第 28A 條又把它延伸到「和／或存活」；兩套系統在同一份文件裡是分開掛理由的，這張圖也把它們分開畫。再下面一段是兩套系統疊起來看會看到什麼：一個 4,881 名 55 歲以下成人分化型甲狀腺癌的登記，1980 到 2016 年初次治療，中位追蹤 6.6 年，122 人（2.5%）死於這個病，把 AJCC 第八版的期別、2015 年版三級復發風險與年齡三個維度交叉，終點是 10 年疾病特異性存活——注意這張表的終點是存活，它是拿復發風險去把存活估得更細——畫成六條橫條：第一期加復發風險低 100%、第一期加中風險 98%、第一期加高風險且 45 歲以下 95%、第一期加高風險且 45 到 55 歲 89%、第二期加高風險且 45 歲以下 78%、第二期加高風險且 45 到 55 歲 61%。說明寫：同樣都寫「第八版第一期」，從 100% 到 89%；同樣都寫「第八版第二期」，從 78% 到 61%；原作者自己的結論是第八版把多達三分之一的病人重新歸進比較年輕的預後分組，低期別裡的疾病光譜因此變寬，那些樂觀的估計未必反映得了帶有高風險特徵的個別病人。接著一格寫第八版對復發也分得比較好、但那是另一個終點：一項納入 3,248 名治療後無病者的登記研究，終點是復發，其中 110 人（3%）復發、中位 27 個月；用第七版排，第二期相對第一期的風險比是 0.91（95% 信賴區間 0.39–2.11），幾乎沒有差別，換成第八版，第二期的風險比變成 4.06（2.38–6.93）；這是好消息，但不要把它和上一段的存活數字混在同一句話裡，那一段的終點是死亡，這一段的終點是復發。再一格寫分期系統本來就解釋不了多少：2015 年版指引寫過，所有為預測甲狀腺癌死亡而設計的分期系統能解釋的不確定性都只有 5% 到 30%，復發風險系統則是 19% 到 34%；就算期別和風險組都排好，大部分的不確定性仍然留在外面，所以期別不是一個結論，它是一個起點。圖的最後是一個紅框的界線區塊，標題是「這張圖不會替你把兩個標籤合成一個」，內容有六條：兩條軸之間不畫箭頭，「第一期」不等於「低風險」、「中間—高風險」也不是「第三期」，任何把兩個標籤合成一句話的說法都是錯的；「一把尺量死亡、一把尺量復發」那種對稱的講法，指引沒說過後面那半句，這張圖不寫，不對稱只成立在一個方向——分期是為死亡建的、指引自己說它不足以預測復發，而第 28A 條把復發分層延伸到「和／或存活」；每一個數字都帶版本，AJCC 第七版用 45 歲、第八版用 55 歲，美國甲狀腺學會 2015 年版用的是第七版、2025 年版才是這個學會第一份以第八版為基礎的分化型甲狀腺癌指引；網路上最常看到的「甲狀腺癌五年存活率 98%」來源通常是美國的統計，美國預防服務工作小組 2017 年那份文件引用的是 98.1%，那是所有組織型、所有期別、所有年齡合在一起的數字，可以描述一個國家、不能描述你那一格；台灣的分期別數字在全國癌症登記報告裡查無列項，甲狀腺癌沒有期別分布、也沒有分期別的存活，所以這張圖給不出「台灣第幾期活多久」，也不用國外的數字冒充；如果你 55 歲以下而報告寫著第二期，一定要問出口：這是因為有遠端轉移嗎？轉移在哪裡？
en_alt: Schematic drawing the two labels on a thyroid cancer report as two separate axes, divided by a dashed rule, with no arrow of any kind joining them. The figure states first that the two systems were built for different main questions and that the asymmetry holds in one direction only: stage is built for death, the guideline says outright that it is not enough to predict recurrence, and that is exactly why a separate recurrence stratification was made. On the left is axis one, AJCC / TNM stage, which predicts death from this disease, that is disease-specific survival. This column quotes the 2025 American Thyroid Association guidelines for differentiated thyroid cancer: AJCC and UICC staging is designed to predict disease-specific survival and therefore does not predict the overall risk of structural persistence or recurrence. Next comes the age cutoff: the AJCC 8th edition took effect in 2018 and moved the staging age cutoff from 45 to 55; the staging tables in the 2015 edition of these guidelines are still on the 7th edition with the cutoff written as 45, and the 2025 edition is this society's first differentiated thyroid cancer guideline built on the 8th; reading data from before 2018 against a report written today gives the wrong answer. A red-bordered cell carries the sentence in the 8th edition that is misread most often: all patients younger than 55 have stage I disease unless they have distant metastases, in which case their disease is stage II. Read the other way round, if someone under 55 is given "stage II" then by definition distant metastases are already present, and "only stage II" does not exist here. Below that is the layout for patients 55 and over: tumour confined to the thyroid with no metastases is stage I; nodal metastases, or a tumour larger than 4 cm, or gross invasion of the strap muscles make it stage II; gross invasion of subcutaneous soft tissue, larynx, trachea, oesophagus or recurrent laryngeal nerve is stage III; invasion of the prevertebral fascia or encasement of the carotid artery is stage IVA, and distant metastases stage IVB. A note records two further changes in the 8th edition: extrathyroidal extension seen only under the microscope no longer counts towards T3, and nodal metastasis no longer pushes a patient into stage III automatically. The shift between editions follows: a meta-analysis of 6 studies and 10,850 patients with differentiated thyroid cancer, median follow-up 55 to 148 months, staged the same patients once under each edition. Two stacked bars and four lines of figures give stage I 60% to 81%, stage II 5% to 13%, stage III 21% to 2%, and stage IV 10% to 3%. Ten-year disease-specific survival from the same analysis is set out by edition: stage II is 98.1% (96.6-99.6) under the 7th edition and 88.6% (82.7-94.6) under the 8th; stage III is 96.8% (94.1-99.64) under the 7th and 70.5% (59.1-83.9) under the 8th. The note explains that the figure falls by almost ten percentage points not because the patients got worse but because the people put into the box marked "stage II" are a different group, the guideline putting it as 20% to 30% of patients downstaged relative to the 7th edition, so that two reports both saying "stage II" describe different situations if they are on different editions. On the right is axis two, the four-tier ATA recurrence risk, which predicts structural disease persistence or recurrence, locoregionally and/or distantly, and/or survival. This column quotes the reason given in the 2015 edition: because AJCC and TNM staging, built for the risk of death, could not adequately predict the risk of recurrence in differentiated thyroid cancer, the 2009 edition of the guidelines proposed a separate recurrence-risk stratification. The four tiers are defined by the probability of recurrence itself and are drawn as a four-step ladder: low, under 10%; low-intermediate, 10% to 15%; intermediate-high, 16% to 30%; high, over 30%. The note explains that the 2015 edition had three tiers, low, intermediate and high, that the 2025 edition has four, and that the guideline gives its own reason for the split, namely that the conditions gathered in the old intermediate box did not all predict the same risk of recurrence; the tier names are copied verbatim from the guideline. Beneath that is a cell giving what recommendation 28A of the 2025 edition asks this system to determine, verbatim: to determine the risk of structural disease persistence or recurrence, locoregionally and/or distantly, and/or survival, a strong recommendation on moderate certainty evidence. Its note says that "and/or survival" tends to fall off in the retelling but is in the text, so the recurrence system's main job is structural recurrence and the guideline's own recommendation extends it to survival as well, while the sentence pointing the other way - that recurrence risk cannot predict death - the guideline never wrote. The column closes with a yellow cell saying plainly that the full entry conditions for each of the four 2025 tiers could not be obtained, because in the guideline they are a figure and the only extractable text is the four percentage bands, so that for what puts a patient in which tier the only citable table is the 2015 one: low risk requires no aggressive variant, no vascular invasion and no clinical nodal metastases; intermediate risk covers microscopic invasion of perithyroidal soft tissue, aggressive variants, papillary carcinoma with vascular invasion and clinically apparent nodal metastases; high risk covers gross extrathyroidal extension, incomplete resection, distant metastases, metastatic nodes 3 cm and larger, and follicular carcinoma with extensive vascular invasion. The dashed rule between the two columns is labelled "Between the two axes: no arrow". Below both columns sits a hatched box struck through with a cross, headed "No arrow here", beside text saying that the two labels cannot be translated into each other, that "stage I" is not "low risk" and "intermediate-high risk" is not "stage III", that a stage label is not a recurrence probability and a risk tier is not a probability of dying, that the asymmetry holds in one direction only - stage is built for death, the guideline says outright that it is not enough to predict recurrence, and that is exactly why a separate recurrence stratification was made, while the recurrence system's main job is structural recurrence and recommendation 28A extends it to "and/or survival" - and that the two systems are justified separately within the same document so this figure keeps them separately drawn. The next part shows what appears when the two systems are laid over each other: a registry of 4,881 adults under 55 with differentiated thyroid cancer, first treated between 1980 and 2016, median follow-up 6.6 years, 122 of them (2.5%) dying of the disease, with AJCC 8th edition stage, the 2015 three-tier recurrence risk and age crossed against one another and ten-year disease-specific survival as the endpoint, the figure noting that this table's endpoint is survival and that it uses recurrence risk to sharpen the survival estimate. Six horizontal bars give stage I with low recurrence risk 100%, stage I with intermediate risk 98%, stage I with high risk under 45 years 95%, stage I with high risk at 45 to 55 years 89%, stage II with high risk under 45 years 78%, and stage II with high risk at 45 to 55 years 61%. The note observes that reports all saying "8th edition, stage I" run from 100% to 89% and reports saying "8th edition, stage II" run from 78% to 61%, and quotes the authors' own conclusion that the 8th edition reclassified up to a third of patients into the younger prognostic stage groups, widening the spectrum of disease inside those lower stages, but that those optimistic estimates may not reflect the prognosis of an individual patient carrying high-risk features. A further cell records that the 8th edition also separates recurrence better, but on a different endpoint: a population-based study of 3,248 patients disease-free after treatment, in which 110 (3%) recurred at a median of 27 months, gives a hazard ratio for stage II against stage I of 0.91 (95% confidence interval 0.39-2.11) under the 7th edition, which is almost no difference, and 4.06 (2.38-6.93) under the 8th; that is good news, but it does not belong in the same sentence as the survival figures above, because those had death as their endpoint and this one has recurrence. Another cell records that staging systems never explained very much: the 2015 guidelines say that every staging system designed to predict death from thyroid cancer explains only 5% to 30% of the uncertainty, and recurrence-risk systems 19% to 34%, so that even with stage and risk category settled most of the uncertainty stays outside, and a stage is a starting point rather than a conclusion. The figure ends with a red-bordered block headed "This figure will not merge your two labels into one", holding six statements: no arrow is drawn between the two axes, "stage I" is not "low risk" and "intermediate-high risk" is not "stage III", and any sentence that folds the two labels together is wrong; the tidy symmetrical version - one ruler for death, one for recurrence - is a sentence the guideline never wrote, so this figure does not write it either, the asymmetry holding in one direction only, with stage built for death and the guideline saying outright that it is not enough to predict recurrence, while recommendation 28A extends the recurrence system to "and/or survival"; every figure carries its edition, with the AJCC 7th edition using 45 years and the 8th using 55, the 2015 American Thyroid Association guidelines on the 7th edition and the 2025 edition the first from this society built on the 8th; the "98% five-year survival" seen everywhere online usually comes from American statistics, the figure cited in the 2017 US Preventive Services Task Force document being 98.1%, which is all histologies, all stages and all ages together and can describe a country but not one reader's cell of the table; for Taiwan the national cancer registry report gives no stage distribution and no stage-specific survival for thyroid cancer, so no entry was found and the question of how long a given stage lives in Taiwan is not answered here, with no foreign figure used in its place; and if you are under 55 and your report says stage II, the question has to be asked out loud - is this because there are distant metastases, and where are they?

en_alt: A schematic in four parts, setting out what the rise in thyroid cancer looks like in different countries and where the boundaries of the idea of overdiagnosis lie. The first part is Taiwan. On the left, a line shows notified new cases of thyroid malignancy in the national cancer registry at five points: 1,228 in 1999, 2,433 in 2009, 3,737 in 2015, 4,974 in 2020 and 6,045 in 2023, roughly 4.9 times over twenty-four years. In 2023 the figures were 1,507 men and 4,538 women, and thyroid cancer ranked 11th by incidence in men and 4th in women that year. Beneath the line a note records the peer-reviewed version, which covers women only: the age-standardised incidence rate rose from 7.37 per 100,000 in 1995-1999 to 20.53 in 2015-2019, an annual percentage change of 5.9% (95% confidence interval 5.3 to 6.5), and the authors write in their conclusion that they hypothesise overdiagnosis as the main driver - a hypothesis, not an estimate. On the right, separated by a dashed rule labelled "different denominators - these two may not share an axis", is the mortality end of the same year: 225 people died of thyroid malignancy in 2023, 81 men and 144 women, 0.42% of all cancer deaths, ranked 23rd by mortality in men and 23rd in women; and this is one single year, not a trend line. The same card lists the age-standardised rates on the 2000 world standard population: age-standardised incidence 9.49 in men and 28.12 in women per 100,000, and age-standardised mortality 0.39 in men and 0.50 in women. On being diagnosed women run at roughly three times the male figure; on dying of the disease the gap is down to roughly one point three times. Below this part a crossed-out box reads "a year-by-year age-standardised mortality series for Taiwan": no officially published version was found, so the figure carries no Taiwanese mortality trend line, and the 0.39 and 0.50 cannot be used to claim that mortality has stayed flat. The second part is Korea. A line shows cases in the Korean national registry: 3,407 in 1999, 44,748 in 2012, 25,523 in 2015 and 30,676 in 2019. A note beside it records that between 1999 and 2008 incidence rose 6.4-fold (95% confidence interval 4.9 to 8.4) from 6.4 to 40.7 per 100,000, that 94.4% of the increase were tumours smaller than 20 mm and 97.1% were localised or regional disease. Below the line, three horizontal bars give age-standardised incidence per 100,000: 24.09 in 2005, 74.83 in 2012 and 42.52 in 2015, flat by 2018, with a note that people under 30 showed no significant fall after the 2015 peak and if anything signs of a further rise. Next comes a left-to-right arrow carrying two dated marks: 2012, incidence begins to fall, and 2014, the public debate begins. Beside it the figure quotes the source: the decline ran from 2012 to 2016, before the debates began in 2014; something that happened first cannot be explained by something that happened afterwards; and the curve rose again after 2015 (25,523 cases in 2015, 30,676 in 2019), so the single-line story in which one public statement brings incidence down is not drawn here. This part closes with three bars headed "deaths from thyroid cancer per 1,000 person-years among people already diagnosed with it, set out by year of diagnosis": 1.94 in 2005, 0.76 in 2013 and 2.70 in 2018, with the rise concentrated in two groups, those who had a total thyroidectomy and those who had no thyroid surgery at all. The cohort is a Korean nationwide cohort following 434,228 people already diagnosed with thyroid cancer (352,678 women, 81,550 men), mean age 48.6 years, median follow-up 7.4 years. The figure states that the denominator is people already diagnosed and not the population, a different calculation from the per-100,000 rates above, so the two lines are not comparable; in the years when screening poured large numbers of low-risk people into that denominator the mortality within this group of course fell and rose again once screening receded, so all it can speak to is that the composition of the people being diagnosed changed, and it cannot speak for the population; the authors themselves write that this line is discordant with Korean population mortality, which continuously decreased until 2015. The third part is the United States: a grey panel records that the 2025 guidelines state that between 1974 and 2013 the rise in incidence occurred across all stages, and that over the same period the mortality rate increased annually by 1.1% in advanced disease; the same document also records that after United States incidence peaked at 14.9 per 100,000 in 2015, the years 2015 to 2017 brought the first decline in three decades. So "more of it, and no more deaths" is a stronger sentence than the evidence behind it; what rebuts it is the American line, that the cell in which mortality rose is advanced disease. As for how overall mortality moved across countries, there is no series here to cite, so none is drawn. The fourth part is the 63-country estimate covering 2013 to 2017, 63 countries and 385 cancer registries. One long horizontal bar is split in two, the larger segment labelled: of 2,297,057 cases, 1,736,133 (75.6%) were attributed to overdiagnosis, of whom 1,368,181 were women and 367,952 were men. Two tags record that the female overdiagnosis fraction exceeded 85% in Cyprus, China, South Korea and Turkiye, and was estimated at zero in Uganda, Zimbabwe and Trinidad and Tobago. The same panel notes that the international gap between the highest and lowest female incidence had widened to 101.4 per 100,000 by 2012 while the international gap in mortality stayed at roughly 1.0 to 2.0 per 100,000 throughout, and it states plainly that the 75.6% is the number of people diagnosed in a whole country minus the number who would have developed symptoms, an arithmetic with no cell in it for you. A second crossed-out box below reads "a Taiwanese overdiagnosis percentage": the abstract of that paper does not name Taiwan, the full text is not open access and the supplementary material could not be obtained, so no Taiwanese overdiagnosis percentage appears on this figure and no other country is used to stand in for one. The figure ends with a red-framed panel headed "what this figure must not be read to say". Overdiagnosis is not misdiagnosis; the pathologist did not get it wrong and those really are cancer cells. Nor does it mean the thing is not really cancer; it is about whether this cancer would ever have caused trouble in this person's remaining lifetime. It can only be worked out at the level of a population and only in retrospect - the number of people diagnosed minus the number of the same people who would have developed symptoms - and no test can tell you today whether your nodule belongs to that difference. So "three-quarters of cases worldwide were attributed to overdiagnosis" cannot be rewritten as "mine probably needs no attention"; what actually decides is the histological type, the size, the invasion, the nodes on your report and your age, which are covered in "Papillary, follicular, NIFTP: reading the report" and "Why the stage depends on your age". The opposite reading is barred too: the figure does not say that finding things early is all superfluous, because mortality in the advanced-disease cell has been moving and high-risk groups were never inside the scope of the 2017 US Preventive Services Task Force grade D recommendation, which is about asymptomatic adults.

1.519（1.038 到 2.222），兩個區間都在 1 的右邊；而永久性副甲狀腺低下、永久性聲帶麻痺與復發這三項區間都跨過 1，看不出差別。同一段另引 2025 年一份納入 21 篇、9,397 人的統合分析：監測期間疾病進展率 14.53%（95% 信賴區間 9.59 到 2025 最直接——沒有照著追蹤走，這個做法的安全性主張就不成立。接著一格寫「而且沒有終點」：三份指引都說不知道監測要做多久、幾歲可以停，日本那份的結論是終身監測，美國那份寫必要的追蹤長度仍然未知。圖的最後是一個紅框的「這張圖不能被讀成什麼」：不能讀成「先觀察看著」；不能讀成「日本人都這樣做」；不能讀成「觀察比較安全」；不能讀成「幾乎不會長大」（未滿 40 歲的 10 年進展率是 22.5%，20 幾歲的終身進展機率是 60.3%）；也不要把「撐住不要開刀」當成目標。開刀的範圍指向〈半切還是全切〉，結節本身怎麼分格指向〈照到一顆結節，然後呢〉，甲狀腺球蛋白怎麼讀指向〈追蹤看的是超音波和一個數字〉。最下面列出想走這條路可以照著念的五個問句：我這顆是不是 cT1a、有沒有貼著氣管或往後面長；如果進監測，第一次超音波排幾個月後、誰照、你們有沒有追蹤提醒的機制；長到幾毫米你會叫我開刀；我這個歲數終身進展的機率落在哪一格；如果我開始睡不著，我可以隨時說我要開刀嗎。
en_alt: A schematic that breaks active surveillance for low-risk papillary microcarcinoma into seven parts, to show that it is a set of written conditions rather than "let us watch and see". The first part is inclusion, in three cards side by side. American Thyroid Association 2025, recommendation 11A: the option is restricted to cT1aN0M0 papillary carcinoma - tumour 1 cm or smaller, no clinically suspicious neck nodes, no distant metastasis - as a conditional recommendation with low-certainty evidence, which in plain words means it may be done but the research holding it up is not of high quality. Korean Thyroid Association 2025, four conditions that must all hold at once: a fine-needle report of Bethesda category V or VI and 1 cm or smaller; no clinical nodal or distant metastasis; no obvious invasion of the strap muscles, trachea or recurrent laryngeal nerve on imaging; and none of the aggressive subtypes - tall cell, columnar cell, hobnail, solid or diffuse sclerosing. The same document recommends surgery for everyone under 19. The Japan Association of Endocrine Surgery consensus of 2021 lists seven further situations that go straight to surgery, of which the figure names two: the tumour sitting against the trachea and possibly already invading it, and the tumour lying on the course of the recurrent laryngeal nerve. That document states that evidence grading does not apply to it, so it carries no grade; and position sometimes matters more than size, since among papillary microcarcinomas smaller than 7 mm not one invaded the trachea or the recurrent laryngeal nerve at surgery. Next come the data above 1 cm: a single Japanese centre with a T1b cohort of only 61 people who chose surveillance; one American academic centre that widened the ceiling to 2 cm with 112 people under surveillance and a mean follow-up of 37.1 months; and the New York cohort of 291 people with intrathyroidal tumours up to 1.5 cm. Below them a crossed-out box reads "1.5 cm or 2 cm can be watched too": a few centres, a few people, short follow-up, and the ceiling that holds is 1 cm. This part closes with a gold panel stating that active surveillance is not something that has been proved but something that is permitted: the commissioned systematic review gathered seven studies comparing active surveillance with immediate surgery and seven further uncontrolled treatment series, only one study being rated "fair" and all the rest "poor", the source not saying whether that rating covers only the seven comparative studies or all fourteen, with the conclusion that methodological limitations prevent any strong conclusion; and while the 2021 Korean imaging consensus advises against biopsy first for certain highly suspicious nodules under 1 cm, being allowed to skip the needle is not the same as being allowed to decide alone. The second part is what is looked at during surveillance: neck ultrasound every 6 months for the first 1 to 2 years, then yearly if there is no progression, the same interval in all three documents. Beside it a second crossed-out box reads "measuring thyroglobulin during surveillance": recommendation 13 of the 2025 edition states that thyroglobulin is not measured during surveillance, nor are its antibodies, listed as good practice which the guideline does not grade, because the thyroid is still there intact and the number has no baseline against which to be read. The third part is the exit conditions, in two cards. The tumour side: growth of the primary by 3 mm or more; new biopsy-proven nodal metastasis; distant metastasis; extrathyroidal extension; and posterior growth, because behind the thyroid sit the trachea and the recurrent laryngeal nerve. The person side, written into the same recommendation rather than as a footnote: patient anxiety, inability to attend follow-up, and the patient saying they want surgery. A note records that the fourth Korean exit condition is simply that the patient chooses surgery, at the highest strength of recommendation; that growth must be present on two consecutive examinations at least 6 months apart; and that the Japanese size threshold is 13 mm. The fourth part is the probability of progression, in two cards. On the left, bars of the lifetime probability from the original Kuma paper (1,211 patients aged 20 to 79, estimated on surveillance to age 85): 60.3% in their twenties, 37.1% in their thirties, 27.3% in their forties, 14.9% in their fifties, 9.9% in their sixties and 3.5% in their seventies, with a note that the Japanese consensus transcribing the same paper lists a different and lower set that does not reconcile, and that what is drawn is the original abstract. On the right, ten-year progression by age in 1,235 Japanese patients: 22.5% under 40, 4.9% at 40 to 59 and 2.5% at 60 and over, with a note that progression there means growth to 12 mm or more or new nodal metastasis, not death. Three further cohorts are listed: Kuma Hospital over 30 years with 3,222 patients (growth of 3 mm or more in 3.8%, 4.7% at ten years, 6.6% at twenty; new nodal metastasis 0.8%, 1.0% at ten years, 1.6% at twenty; no thyroid cancer deaths); a Korean prospective cohort of 706 (composite progression 5.3% at two years and 14.2% at five, odds ratio 2.86 with 95% confidence interval 1.10 to 7.45 for those under 30); and the New York cohort of 291 (3.8% grew by 3 mm or more, cumulative 12.1% at five years, no regional or distant metastasis). The fifth part is who leaves. It quotes the 2025 guidelines - driven more by patient choice than signs of progression - and explains that the proportion going on to surgery varies between centres. A bar divided into five segments then shows the Japanese data on 2,288 people, of whom 162 (7.1%) converted to surgery after 12 months: disease progression 57, patient preference 43, physician preference 31, other thyroid or parathyroid disease 24, and other 7. Beside it, a Korean multicentre cohort of 370 in which 58 (15.7%) had delayed surgery, the commonest reason being anxiety at 37.9%, then tumour growth at 32.8% and nodal metastasis at 8.6%. A closing line says this is not failure: anxiety severe enough to affect daily life is written into the exit conditions, and holding out against surgery is not the goal. The sixth part is the price of operating later, drawn as intervals on a logarithmic axis with a dashed line marked "1 = no difference": delayed surgery gives transient hypoparathyroidism an odds ratio of 1.705 (95% confidence interval 1.188 to 2.448) and transient vocal cord palsy 1.519 (1.038 to 2.222), both intervals lying to the right of 1, while permanent hypoparathyroidism, permanent vocal cord palsy and recurrence all have intervals crossing 1 with no difference visible. The same part cites a 2025 meta-analysis of 21 studies and 9,397 people: disease progression during surveillance 14.53% (95% confidence interval 9.59 to 21.43) with no thyroid cancer deaths in either group, but with overall complications and recurrence both higher in the delayed-surgery group and a conclusion that active surveillance should be undertaken with caution. The seventh part is that the place doing this has conditions too. Ideal: an experienced multidisciplinary team, high-quality neck ultrasound, prospective data collection and a follow-up reminder system. Not suitable: reliable neck ultrasound unavailable or little experience of thyroid cancer, and on the patient side anyone unlikely to attend follow-up. The Japanese consensus requires a multidisciplinary team including an imaging specialist experienced in neck ultrasound as a necessary condition. The Korean Society of Thyroid Radiology requires a high-quality neck ultrasound by a specialist before starting, with "ideal / acceptable / not suitable" written into the report. The 2025 American guideline is the most direct: if the follow-up is not actually carried out, the safety claim for this approach does not hold. A panel beneath adds that there is no end point - all three guidelines say they do not know how long surveillance should run or at what age it may stop, the Japanese document concluding with lifelong surveillance and the American one writing that the necessary duration of follow-up remains unknown. The figure ends with a red-framed panel of readings that are barred: it does not say "let us watch and see"; it does not say "this is what the Japanese do"; it does not say watching is safer; it does not say the tumour hardly ever grows, since ten-year progression under 40 is 22.5% and the lifetime probability in their twenties is 60.3%; and holding out against surgery is not the goal. How much gland comes out is covered in "Half the gland, or all of it", how the nodule itself is sorted in "A scan found a nodule. Now what?", and how thyroglobulin is read in "Follow-up is an ultrasound and one number". At the foot are five questions to read out before taking this road: is mine cT1a and is it against the trachea or growing backwards; if I go into surveillance, how many months until the first ultrasound, who performs it, and do you have a follow-up reminder system; at how many millimetres would you tell me to have surgery; at my age, which cell does my lifetime probability of progression fall in; and if I start losing sleep over this, may I say at any point that I want surgery.

公分那一格，單葉切除「可能是比較好的起始治療」，有條件建議、低到中等確定性，理由是風險與副作用明顯較低，但病人與治療團隊也可能選全切，以便做放射碘或讓追蹤好讀。第 15C 條：腫瘤大於 4 公分、任何大小但有明顯甲狀腺外侵犯、臨床上看得到淋巴結轉移、或已有遠端轉移，起始手術要包含全甲狀腺切除，強烈建議、中等確定性。底下一格對照 2015 年版第 35B 條：腫瘤大於 1 公分、小於 4 公分、沒有甲狀腺外侵犯、臨床上沒有淋巴結轉移的人，起始手術可以做雙側也可以做單側，對低風險的乳突癌與濾泡癌單葉切除「可能就足夠」，強烈建議、中等品質證據；關鍵字是「可以」，2025 年版在 2 公分以內那一格把它換成了「應該」。第二段是一個打叉的方框，寫著「一個把半切對全切隨機起來的試驗」：唯一登記在案的隨機嘗試是一個美國中心的可行性先導研究，主要終點寫的是符合資格的病人有多少比例願意入組，試驗登記上的實際收案數是 2 人、2026 年 1 月結案，而登記表給的是收案人數，沒有另外給隨機分派的人數。旁邊寫 2025 年版指引自述：因為低風險分化型甲狀腺癌的結果普遍良好、又缺乏隨機對照試驗，委員會認為必須倚賴大型資料庫研究。第三段是資料庫。一張對數軸的區間圖，中間一條虛線標「1＝看不出差別」，三條區間是2014 年那篇用美國癌症資料庫重做的分析（1998 到 2006 年、腫瘤 1.0 到 4.0 公分的乳突癌 61,775 人，中位追蹤 82 個月，校正後的整體存活）：全部 1.0 到 4.0 公分風險比 0.96（95% 信賴區間 0.84 到 1.09）、1.0 到 2.0 公分 1.05（0.88 到 1.26）、2.1 到 4.0 公分 0.89（0.73 到 1.07），三個區間都壓在 1 附近；2015 年另一篇看未滿 45 歲、第 I 期、1.1 到 4.0 公分的人結果也一樣。同一段引 2007 年那篇 52,173 位乳突癌的分析：小於 1 公分時手術範圍不影響復發或存活，1 公分以上單葉切除的復發與死亡風險比較高，只看 1 到 2 公分那一格也一樣。接著三條但書：終點是整體存活不是疾病特異性存活，而分化型甲狀腺癌的病人多半死於別的原因；兩組本來就不是同一群人，2014 年那篇裡接受全切的人淋巴結轉移 27%、單葉切除組 7%，甲狀腺外侵犯 16% 比 5%，多發病灶 44% 比 29%，這叫適應症造成的混淆；以及 2015 年那篇的「第 I 期」用的是 AJCC 第七版的 45 歲切點，不是第八版的 55 歲。第四段是半切之後要不要吃藥。兩張並排卡片：目標訂在正常參考範圍時，單葉切除後不必補充甲狀腺素的比例是七到八成；目標訂在舊版那個偏低的區間時只剩兩到三成。2025 年版寫，復發風險落在低或中度那兩格的人（這裡用的是舊的三級講法），不論做的是全切還是單葉切除，促甲狀腺素的目標就是正常參考範圍。底下一格標明「下面這幾個世代用的門檻都是舊目標那條線」，三條橫條：一年內 TSH 升到 2 mIU/L 以上 73%（一個 555 例單葉切除的世代裡，術前沒吃藥的 478 人中有 350 人）；因惡性而切者用了甲狀腺素 59.3%（全美理賠資料裡的 33,756 例單葉切除，因良性而切的是 39.4%，校正後勝算比 2.34，95% 信賴區間 2.20 到 2.48，那份資料沒有告訴我們目標各自訂在哪裡）；單葉切除後被診斷為甲狀腺低下 22%（2012 年一篇 32 篇研究的統合分析，95% 信賴區間 19 到 27，能分清楚的只有其中 4 篇，估計亞臨床 12%、臨床 4%，這一筆混合良性與惡性，終點是有沒有被診斷為甲狀腺低下、不是有沒有吃藥，2025 年版轉述時把 22% 標成生化性低下、和原文不一樣，這裡引的是原文）。再底下列出誰比較容易在術後被驗出甲狀腺低下：術前 TSH 大於 2.5 的人相對風險 3.16（2.03 到 4.90）、甲狀腺抗體陽性 3.52、病理上有甲狀腺炎 3.30；這一組的終點是被診斷為甲狀腺低下，不是開始吃藥。第五段是補全切：回溯研究 5% 到 43%、統合分析 11% 到 34%、術中因為發現高風險特徵而當場轉成全切約 21%、依最終病理補做全切約 27% 到 30%；2025 年版直接寫了一句要讓病人事先知道的話——有至少兩成的可能會在術中轉成全切、或之後補做全切。第二次手術的風險有兩筆：一個 786 人的單一機構世代裡，先單葉再補全切的 149 人暫時性副甲狀腺低下反而比一次做完全切的 637 人少；另一份 70,638 人的全國手術品質登錄裡兩者的 30 天死亡率都是 0.1%、整體併發症也相當，但那份登錄不收錄副甲狀腺低下與喉返神經麻痺。第六段是兩邊各要付什麼，兩張並排卡片中間一條虛線。全切相對於單葉切除，統合分析算出來的相對風險是暫時性低血鈣接近十倍、永久性低血鈣約三倍、喉返神經傷害與術後出血都落在一點七到二點六之間；這張圖刻意不給絕對百分比，因為那些數字取決於那家醫院怎麼查喉、以及把幾個月算成永久。半切這一側：有機會走到第二次手術；2025 年版寫單葉切除之後的復發大多出現在對側那一葉，多半靠補做全切救得回來；日本一個 30 年的世代裡 1,327 位接受單葉切除的低風險乳突微小癌病人中有 18 人（1.4%）在殘餘的甲狀腺復發；追蹤不是比較輕鬆，是看的東西不一樣。圖的最後是一個紅框的「這張圖不能被讀成什麼」：「全部切掉比較乾淨」不是這條線的依據；資料庫那幾篇的終點是整體存活而且兩組本來就不是同一群人，看不出差別不等於證明沒有差別；「半切就不用吃藥」要看目標訂在哪；半切能省掉的不是一輩子的藥，而是全切之後必然的終身替代；這張圖不能拿來自己決定切多少，要不要開刀指向〈不開刀先看著，但有條件〉，淋巴結指向〈淋巴結要不要一起清〉，併發症的分母與定義指向〈開完刀會少掉什麼〉，藥要吃到多少指向〈吃一輩子的那顆藥，要吃到多少〉。最下面是五個可以照著念的門診問句：我這顆量起來幾公分、落在 2 公分以內那一格嗎；你評估我需不需要做放射碘、如果需要是不是就得全切；如果術中冰凍或術後病理跑出高風險特徵你會建議我補全切嗎、機率大概多少；如果我半切你會什麼時候幫我驗 TSH、多少以上你會開藥；如果我選半切我需要放棄什麼。
en_alt: A schematic in six parts about how much thyroid to remove in differentiated thyroid cancer. The first part is the line itself, in three cards side by side, following recommendations 15A, 15B and 15C of the 2025 American Thyroid Association guidelines. Recommendation 15A: for a tumour of 2 cm or smaller (cT1) with no gross extrathyroidal extension and no clinical nodal or distant metastasis, the initial operation "should be" a thyroid lobectomy - a strong recommendation with moderate-certainty evidence - unless there is cancer on both sides or another reason the contralateral lobe must come out; the verb in this cell is not "may" but "should". Recommendation 15B: for tumours above 2 cm and up to 4 cm, lobectomy "may be the preferred" initial treatment, a conditional recommendation with low-to-moderate certainty, on the grounds that the risks and side effects are clearly lower, though the patient and team may also choose total thyroidectomy to allow radioiodine or to make follow-up easier to read. Recommendation 15C: for tumours larger than 4 cm, any size with gross extrathyroidal extension, clinically apparent nodal metastasis, or distant metastasis already present, the initial operation should include total thyroidectomy, a strong recommendation with moderate certainty. A panel beneath sets this against recommendation 35B of the 2015 edition: for tumours larger than 1 cm and smaller than 4 cm without extrathyroidal extension and without clinical nodal metastasis, the initial operation could be bilateral or unilateral, and for low-risk papillary and follicular carcinoma a lobectomy "may be sufficient", a strong recommendation with moderate-quality evidence. The operative word was "may"; in the cell at or below 2 cm the 2025 edition replaced it with "should". The second part is a crossed-out box reading "a trial that randomises lobectomy against total thyroidectomy": the only registered randomised attempt was a feasibility pilot at one American centre whose primary endpoint was the proportion of eligible patients willing to enrol, with 2 an actual enrolment count of 2 according to the registry, closing in January 2026, the registry entry giving the number enrolled and no separate number randomised. Beside it, the 2025 guidelines are quoted as saying that because outcomes in low-risk differentiated thyroid cancer are generally good and randomised controlled trials are lacking, the committee had to rely on large database studies. The third part is the databases, drawn as intervals on a logarithmic axis with a dashed line marked "1 = no difference". The three intervals come from the 2014 re-analysis of the American cancer database (61,775 papillary carcinomas of 1.0 to 4.0 cm diagnosed 1998 to 2006, median follow-up 82 months, adjusted overall survival): all tumours 1.0 to 4.0 cm, hazard ratio 0.96 (95% confidence interval 0.84 to 1.09); 1.0 to 2.0 cm, 1.05 (0.88 to 1.26); 2.1 to 4.0 cm, 0.89 (0.73 to 1.07). All three sit close to 1, and a 2015 paper on stage I patients under 45 with tumours of 1.1 to 4.0 cm found the same. The same panel records the 2007 analysis of 52,173 papillary carcinomas, in which the extent of surgery affected neither recurrence nor survival below 1 cm, while above 1 cm lobectomy carried a higher risk of recurrence and of death, including in the 1 to 2 cm cell taken alone. Three caveats follow: the endpoint is overall survival rather than disease-specific survival, and most people with differentiated thyroid cancer die of something else; the two groups were never the same people, since in the 2014 paper nodal metastasis was 27% against 7%, extrathyroidal extension 16% against 5% and multifocal disease 44% against 29%, which is confounding by indication; and the "stage I" of the 2015 paper uses the AJCC seventh edition cut-off of 45 years rather than the eighth edition's 55. The fourth part is whether the tablet is needed after half the gland. Two cards side by side: with the target set at the normal reference range, roughly seven to eight in ten people need no thyroxine after a lobectomy; with the target set at the older, lower range, only two to three in ten. The 2025 edition says that for people whose recurrence risk falls in the low or moderate cells, using the older three-tier wording, the TSH target is the normal reference range whether the operation was total thyroidectomy or lobectomy. A panel below is headed "every cohort below used the old target as its threshold" and carries three bars: TSH above 2 mIU/L within one year, 73% (350 of the 478 patients not already on thyroxine, within a cohort of 555 lobectomies); thyroxine used after lobectomy for malignancy, 59.3% (of 33,756 lobectomies in a national claims dataset, against 39.4% of those done for benign disease, adjusted odds ratio 2.34, 95% confidence interval 2.20 to 2.48, with that dataset not recording where each target was set); and diagnosed hypothyroid after lobectomy, 22% (a 2012 meta-analysis of 32 studies, 95% confidence interval 19 to 27, with only 4 studies separating clinical from subclinical disease at 12% and 4%, mixing benign with malignant, its endpoint being diagnosed hypothyroid rather than taking a tablet, and with the 2025 guidelines labelling that 22% as biochemical where the original does not - what is drawn is the original). Below that, who is more likely to be found hypothyroid afterwards: a preoperative TSH above 2.5, relative risk 3.16 (2.03 to 4.90); positive thyroid antibodies 3.52; thyroiditis on the pathology 3.30 - all with the endpoint of being diagnosed hypothyroid rather than starting thyroxine. The fifth part is completion thyroidectomy: retrospective studies 5% to 43%, meta-analyses 11% to 34%, conversion to total thyroidectomy during the operation for high-risk features about 21%, and completion thyroidectomy on the final pathology about 27% to 30%. The 2025 edition writes one sentence patients are to be told in advance: there is at least a one-in-five chance of conversion during the operation or completion afterwards. Two figures describe the second operation: in a single-institution cohort of 786 people, the 149 who had lobectomy followed by completion thyroidectomy had less transient hypoparathyroidism than the 637 who had a total thyroidectomy in one sitting; and in a national surgical quality registry of 70,638 people, 30-day mortality was 0.1% for both with comparable overall complications, though that registry does not capture hypoparathyroidism or recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy. The sixth part sets the two sides against each other in two cards separated by a dashed rule. Total thyroidectomy against lobectomy, as relative risks from meta-analysis: transient hypocalcaemia close to tenfold, permanent hypocalcaemia about threefold, and recurrent laryngeal nerve injury and postoperative bleeding both between one point seven and two point six; the figure deliberately gives no absolute percentages, because those depend on how the hospital examines the larynx and on how many months count as permanent. The lobectomy side: a second operation is possible; recurrence after lobectomy mostly appears in the contralateral lobe and can usually be retrieved by completion thyroidectomy; in a 30-year Japanese cohort 18 of 1,327 patients (1.4%) who had a lobectomy for low-risk papillary microcarcinoma recurred in the remaining thyroid; and follow-up is not lighter, only different. The figure ends with a red-framed panel of readings that are barred: "taking it all out is cleaner" is not what this line rests on; the database papers measure overall survival and the two groups were never the same people, so no difference seen is not a difference disproved; "half the gland means no tablet" depends on where the target is set; what a lobectomy spares is not a lifetime of tablets but the replacement that is inevitable after the whole gland comes out; and the figure is not a tool for deciding your own extent of surgery - whether to operate at all is in "Watching instead of operating, on conditions", the nodes in "Should the nodes come out too", the denominators and definitions of the complications in "What the operation takes with it", and the dose in "The tablet you take for life, and how much". At the foot are five questions to read out at the clinic: how many centimetres does mine measure and is it in the cell at or below 2 cm; do you think I will need radioiodine and if so does the whole gland have to come out; if the frozen section or final pathology shows high-risk features would you recommend completion thyroidectomy and roughly what is the chance; if I have a lobectomy when will you check my TSH and above what value would you start me on thyroxine; and if I choose the lobectomy, what am I giving up.

2.3%，但同一篇也寫這個報告率會隨著喉部檢查方式不同從 2.3% 一路變到 26%；差距十倍，來源不是手術本身，是有沒有去看。方塊下面掛一個標籤：越認真找的醫院，帳面上的數字越難看。第二條是副甲狀腺低下，文獻上 0.5% 到 65%，來源是另一篇納入 45 篇、23,164 人的系統性回顧。理由方塊寫：那一篇開場第一句就是發生率從 0.5% 到 65% 都有，主要原因是每個研究對它的定義不同，尤其是用幾個月當作暫時與永久的分界；同一篇把兩種切點統一算過，以 6 個月為界的永久性副甲狀腺低下是 4.11%、以 12 個月為界是 4.08%，兩者其實沒有差別，但那是在同一篇分析裡統一算的，不同研究之間仍然不能直接比。方塊下面的標籤是：同一篇內可以比，跨篇不可以比。第三條與第四條是美國甲狀腺學會 2025 年分化型甲狀腺癌指引自己給的區間：暫時性副甲狀腺低下 14% 到 43%、永久性副甲狀腺低下 1% 到 25%。說明寫連指引列的區間也是寬的，寬到看起來不像醫學數字，而它寬的理由就是上面那兩件事；二十五倍的跨度寫在同一句話裡，所以當有人告訴你這個手術的副甲狀腺低下大概是百分之幾，要接著問的是：你說的是暫時還是永久，以及你用幾個月當界線。第二段是三張分母清楚的卡片，每一張都帶著它的世代。第一張是斯堪地那維亞 26 個科、3,660 次手術的登錄（良性與惡性混合）：單側喉返神經麻痺 3.9%、雙側 5.75 到 19.31）、永久性低血鈣 3.17（1.72 到 5.83）、暫時性喉返神經傷害 1.69（1.30 到 2.20）、永久性喉返神經傷害 1.85（1.28 到 2.69）、術後出血 2.58（1.69 到 3.93）；另一份 62,722 例的分析用的是整體併發症，全切 20.4%、單側手術 10.8%。這一組的終點是低血鈣與神經傷害本身，分母是被納入的那些研究，不是任何一家醫院。第四段是手術量的門檻，同樣不是一個數字，三張並排的卡片：美國甲狀腺學會 2025 年版第 6 條寫每年超過 25 到 50 例（強烈建議、中等確定性），理由是高量的甲狀腺外科醫師平均而言併發症較低、結果較好，甲狀腺癌病人應該被提供轉介給高量外科醫師的選項，尤其是需要較大範圍手術的腫瘤，而它給的是一個區間不是一個數字；2017 年、16,954 例全切的全國住院樣本算出的轉折點是每年 26 例，一年只做 1 例的醫師併發症勝算增加 87%，2 到 5 例增加 68%、6 到 10 例 42%、11 到 15 例 22%、16 到 20 例 10%、21 到 25 例 3%；英國內分泌與甲狀腺外科登錄要每年超過 50 例才看到下降，最高量組（每年超過 100 例）的永久性副甲狀腺低下 3%、喉返神經麻痺 2.6%，作者自己說這份資料缺失比例高、可能有偏誤。再加上 1998 年一份美國單一州、5,860 次出院的分析：最高量那組住院併發症 5.1%、中間兩組 6.1%、最低量組 8.6%，而且併發症與住院天數比較取決於外科醫師的經驗，醫院的量沒有一致的關聯。這一段的黃色橫幅寫著「26、50、100——三個門檻，一個沒有共識的問題」，並說把這三個數字合成一句「每年至少要做幾例」是不該做的事，它們來自不同的資料庫、不同的年代、不同的併發症定義。第五段回答為什麼要一直抽血驗鈣：2018 年那份專門講術後副甲狀腺低下的聲明寫得很清楚，它指的是副甲狀腺素低、同時血鈣也低，兩個要一起成立；術後副甲狀腺素低於 15 pg/mL 代表急性副甲狀腺低下的風險升高；同一份列的風險因子是雙側手術、自體免疫甲狀腺疾病、中央區淋巴結廓清、胸骨後甲狀腺腫、外科醫師經驗不足與吸收不良；2025 年版第 24B 條寫全切或中央區廓清之後應該依副甲狀腺素給鈣與維生素 D，這樣比單純觀察加連續驗血鈣更能降低低血鈣、縮短住院，強烈建議、中等確定性。圖的最後是一個紅框的界線區塊，標題是「這張圖不給你一個可以拿去比醫院的百分比」，內容四條：每一個報告率都要帶怎麼查與怎麼定義，少掉任何一件兩家醫院的數字就不可比；瑞典那兩篇的世代是因為良性甲狀腺疾病接受全切的人、不是甲狀腺癌，4,899 人中 246 人（5.2%）有永久性副甲狀腺低下、平均追蹤 4.4 年、校正後死亡風險比 2.09（95% 信賴區間 1.04 到 4.20），同一個登錄另一篇 4,828 人腎功能不全的風險比 4.88（2.00 到 11.95）、本來就有心血管疾病的人心血管事件風險比 1.88（1.02 到 3.47），這些數字不外推到癌症，只能告訴我們永久性副甲狀腺低下不是小事；這張圖不給鈣片與活性維生素 D 的劑量或天數，那要照你手術醫院的術後補鈣流程走，2025 年版也把術前的聲音評估列為強烈建議、中等確定性；最後是術前門診可以照著念的兩句問句，以及出院那天要問到的兩個數字——我今天的血鈣和副甲狀腺素各是多少。
en_alt: Schematic on one subject: why the same complication is reported as two percentages that differ by a factor of ten. The figure runs in five parts. The first part draws the two headline ranges on one shared scale from zero to seventy per cent. All four bars are drawn as ranges with end caps; no median and no mean stands in for the span. The first bar is recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy, reported at 2.3% to 26%, from a systematic review of 27 studies and about 25,000 patients. The reason block beside it explains that the same review gives mean rates of 9.8% for transient palsy and 2.3% for permanent palsy, while also stating that the reported rate runs from 2.3% all the way to 26% depending on how the larynx was examined; a tenfold spread whose source is not the operation but whether anyone went and looked. A tag underneath reads: the harder a unit looks, the worse its figures read. The second bar is hypoparathyroidism, reported in the literature at 0.5% to 65%, from a second systematic review of 45 studies and 23,164 patients. Its reason block records that the review opens with exactly this - incidence from 0.5% to 65%, mainly because each study defines it differently and above all because they differ on how many months separate transient from permanent - and that the same review recalculated both cutoffs on one consistent basis, giving permanent hypoparathyroidism of 4.11% on a six-month cutoff and 4.08% on a twelve-month cutoff, which is no difference at all, although that comparison holds only inside one analysis and not between separate studies. Its tag reads: comparable within one analysis, not across analyses. The third and fourth bars are the ranges the 2025 American Thyroid Association guidelines for differentiated thyroid cancer give for themselves: transient hypoparathyroidism 14% to 43% and permanent hypoparathyroidism 1% to 25%. The notes say that even the range printed in the guideline is a wide one, wide enough that it hardly looks like a medical figure, and that it is wide for the two reasons above; a twenty-five-fold span sits inside a single sentence, so when someone tells you that hypoparathyroidism after this operation runs at a certain percentage, the question to ask next is whether they mean transient or permanent, and how many months they are calling permanent. The second part is three cards that do have denominators, each read with its cohort. The first is a Scandinavian audit of 26 departments and 3,660 operations, mixing benign and malignant disease: unilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy 3.9%, bilateral palsy 0.2%, still palsied at six months 0.97%, postoperative bleeding 2.1% and postoperative infection 1.6%, with an odds ratio of 8.18 for infection after nodal surgery, and, among the 1,648 bilateral procedures, hypocalcaemia needing active vitamin D in 9.9% at the first clinic visit and 4.4% at six months. This audit is also the source of the finding that routine laryngoscopy is itself an independent associated factor for unilateral vocal cord palsy, odds ratio 1.92. The second card is one high-volume surgeon with 2,527 nerves at risk and fibreoptic laryngoscopy before and after surgery in every patient: vocal fold motion impairment 2.9% and permanent impairment in 9 patients (0.4%), three of whom had the nerve deliberately divided during the operation because the cancer had invaded it. This is the lower end of the range under conditions where everybody is examined - what the left-hand end of the bar above actually looks like. The third card is a long-term voice survey of 308 respondents at a median of 10.7 years after surgery, with anyone carrying a recorded nerve injury deliberately excluded: 113 (37%) self-reported voice problems, but only 22 of them (7.1%) scored above the survey's abnormal cutoff. The commonest complaints were that the clarity of the voice is unpredictable at 23%, that people cannot hear them in a noisy place at 23%, and that they feel they have to strain to produce their voice at 21%. The card closes by saying that quoting only the 37% frightens people while quoting only the 7.1% leaves anyone with symptoms feeling they are making a fuss, and that the 2025 guideline text puts long-term voice change without nerve injury at over 30%. The third part shows how the extent of surgery changes the whole set. A meta-analysis gives relative risks for total thyroidectomy against lobectomy: transient hypocalcaemia 10.67 (95% confidence interval 5.75 to 19.31), permanent hypocalcaemia 3.17 (1.72 to 5.83), transient recurrent laryngeal nerve injury 1.69 (1.30 to 2.20), permanent nerve injury 1.85 (1.28 to 2.69) and postoperative bleeding 2.58 (1.69 to 3.93). A separate analysis of 62,722 operations uses overall complications instead, at 20.4% for total thyroidectomy against 10.8% for unilateral surgery. The endpoints here are hypocalcaemia and nerve injury themselves and the denominator is the studies included, not any one hospital. The fourth part draws the surgeon-volume threshold as three thresholds on three cards. Recommendation 6 of the 2025 American Thyroid Association guidelines gives more than 25 to 50 per year, a strong recommendation with moderate certainty, on the grounds that high-volume thyroid surgeons have on average fewer complications and better outcomes and that patients should be offered the option of referral to one, particularly for tumours needing more extensive surgery - and what it gives is a range, not a number. A 2017 national inpatient sample of 16,954 total thyroidectomies puts the inflection point at 26 per year, with a surgeon performing 1 case a year having 87% higher odds of a complication, 2 to 5 cases 68%, 6 to 10 cases 42%, 11 to 15 cases 22%, 16 to 20 cases 10% and 21 to 25 cases 3%. The United Kingdom registry of endocrine and thyroid surgery sees a decline only above 50 cases a year, with permanent hypoparathyroidism of 3% and recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy of 2.6% in the highest-volume band of more than 100 a year, and its authors say the proportion of missing data is high and the figures may be biased. A note adds a 1998 analysis of 5,860 discharges from a single American state, where the highest-volume group had 5.1% inpatient complications, the middle two 6.1% and the lowest-volume group 8.6%, and where complications and length of stay depended on the surgeon's experience with no consistent association for hospital volume. A yellow banner reads "26, 50, 100 - three thresholds, one question with no agreed answer", and says that folding those three numbers into one sentence about a minimum annual caseload is not something to do, because they come from different databases, different eras and different definitions of complication. The fifth part answers why the blood tests for calcium keep coming. The 2018 statement devoted to postoperative hypoparathyroidism defines it as a low parathyroid hormone level together with a low calcium level, both at once; a postoperative parathyroid hormone below 15 pg/mL indicates a raised risk of acute hypoparathyroidism; and the same statement lists the risk factors as bilateral surgery, autoimmune thyroid disease, central neck dissection, retrosternal goitre, limited surgical experience and malabsorption. Recommendation 24B of the 2025 guideline says that after total thyroidectomy or central neck dissection calcium and vitamin D should be given according to the parathyroid hormone level, which reduces hypocalcaemia and shortens hospital stay better than observation with serial calcium measurements alone; strong recommendation, moderate certainty. The figure ends with a red-bordered block headed "This figure does not give you a percentage you can use to compare hospitals", holding four statements. Every reported rate has to carry how it was looked for and how it was defined, and without either one two hospitals' figures stop being comparable. The two Swedish papers are cohorts of people operated on for benign thyroid disease rather than cancer: of 4,899 patients, 246 (5.2%) had permanent hypoparathyroidism and over a mean follow-up of 4.4 years the adjusted mortality hazard ratio was 2.09 (95% confidence interval 1.04 to 4.20), while a second paper from the same registry of 4,828 patients gives 4.88 (2.00 to 11.95) for renal insufficiency and 1.88 (1.02 to 3.47) for cardiovascular events in those with pre-existing cardiovascular disease; those numbers are not carried across to cancer, and what they do say is that permanent hypoparathyroidism is not a trivial thing. The figure gives no dose and no duration for calcium tablets or active vitamin D, which follow the protocol of the operating hospital, and the 2025 guideline makes preoperative voice assessment a strong recommendation with moderate certainty. Finally, two sentences to read out at the preoperative clinic - do you scope every patient after surgery or only those with symptoms, and how many months on active vitamin D do you count as permanent - and two numbers to ask for on the day of discharge: what is my calcium today, and what is my parathyroid hormone.

IoN；說明寫兩個都是非劣性設計，而且事先講定的那個幅度都是五個百分點，非劣性試驗不能證明無效，它能說的是「不比較差」。ESTIMABL2（法國）那張卡片：隨機分派做放射碘或不做，776 人，全做完全甲狀腺切除；三年無事件比率是不做 95.6%、做 95.9%；五年時 698 人可評估，不做 93.2%、做 94.8%；兩個時間點都在非劣性界限之內。卡片註記寫這裡的「事件」是複合指標，含影像或超音波異常、甲狀腺球蛋白或抗體升高，不是復發，更不是存活。這張卡片裡面另外框了一個紅色方塊，標題是「它排除了誰：這一格必須跟結論寫在同一句裡」，列三條：單顆、一公分以下的乳突微小癌被直接排除，試驗自己寫的理由是這些人本來就不必做；所有淋巴結陽性被排除；pT2 以上被排除。方塊結語寫收進去的是多發但總和一到二公分、或單顆一到二公分、淋巴結陰性或未評估的人，所以它證明的那個「低風險」，不是讀者手上報告的那個低風險。IoN（英國）那張卡片：同樣隨機分派做或不做，33 個中心、504 人，中位追蹤 6.8 與 6.6 年；五年無復發的粗比率是不做 97.9%（96.1 到 99.7）、做 96.3%（93.9 到 98.7）；試驗另外估的五年絕對風險差是 0.5 個百分點（95% 信賴區間 −2.2 到 3.2）。卡片寫明那個 0.5 不是把上面兩個比率相減，它是另外估出來的量，方向是「不做消融多出來的風險」，非劣性成立是因為區間的上界 3.2 落在事先訂好的 5 個百分點界限以內；兩個比率相減是 1.6 個百分點，方向還相反；至於那 0.5 是怎麼估出來的，論文的方法段這次沒有取得，所以講不了。同樣達到非劣性。註記寫它的終點和 ESTIMABL2 不一樣，是局部復發或殘存的結構性疾病、遠端轉移、死於甲狀腺癌合起來算，全程只有 17 次復發；論文自己寫它還在追蹤中，作者的結論比納入條件窄——是 pT1、pT2、淋巴結陰性或未評估、無不良特徵者可以不做。卡片下半是一個小表，標題「試驗裡風險高的人，風險是真的高」：pT3 的 46 人裡 4 人復發（9%）、pT1 或 pT2 的 458 人裡 13 人（3%）、中央區淋巴結陽性的 47 人裡 6 人復發（13%）、陰性或未評估的 457 人裡 11 人（2%）。結語寫論文接著那一句是這些比率在沒做放射碘的人身上是相似的，而全試驗只有 17 個事件，次群組看不出差別不等於沒差別，這是「看不出來」不是「證明沒有」。另一塊的標題是「問題二：要做多少」，放的是 HiLo 與 ESTIMABL1；說明寫這兩個試驗裡每一個人都做了放射碘，隨機分派的是活度高低與準備方式，它們對「要不要做」一個字都沒有回答。HiLo（英國）那張卡片：每一個人都做了放射碘，低活度 1.1 與較高活度 3.7 GBq——這是這兩個試驗的識別特徵，不是誰的處方；主要終點是治療後六到九個月殘餘組織清乾淨，低活度 85.0%、高活度 88.9%；追到中位 6.5 年時七年累積復發率 5.9% 對 7.3%，風險比 1.10（95% 信賴區間 0.47 到 2.59）。註記寫主要終點是替代指標，不是復發也不是存活；結語寫至於你這一次用多少，依你醫院核子醫學科的規定。ESTIMABL1（法國）那張卡片：同樣是每一個人都做了放射碘，隨機分派的是低活度 1.1 與較高活度 3.7 GBq 以及準備方式，主要終點同樣是治療後六到九個月殘餘組織有沒有清乾淨；結語寫把它們拿去回答「要不要做」，是把兩個問題混在一起。兩塊下面是這張圖的重點：同一份指引裡，建議強度的排列是反直覺的。說明先寫 2025 年版把復發風險分成四格，每格掛上機率：低（不到 10%）、低—中間（10 到 15%）、中間—高（16 到 30%）、高（超過 30%），這四個百分比講的是結構性或生化性復發的機率，不是死亡率，也不是期別。接著是四列，每一列寫風險格、建議、強度與確定性：低（不到 10%）——不常規做，強烈建議、高確定性，這一列用粗框標出來；低—中間（10 到 15%）與中間—高（16 到 30%）——可以考慮，有條件建議、低確定性；高（超過 30%）——常規做，強烈建議、中等確定性；一開始就有遠端轉移——要做，強烈建議、中等確定性。黃底橫幅寫：排出來就清楚了，證據最硬的一句是「不要常規做」；指引自己解釋中間那格為什麼講不硬，是單獨針對中間那兩格的研究太少，一份系統性回顧攤得更白、不過它數的是另一批人——舊的三級分層裡被歸為中風險的那一格：11 篇觀察性研究看到好處、13 篇沒有，作者自己還補了一句，其中族群分層做得乾淨的只有少數幾篇；界線後來重畫過，那個中間不等於今天的中間兩格，但分歧的形狀沒有變。再下面一格寫歐洲那份共識：歐洲甲狀腺學會 2022 年的共識同樣把高風險與已知結構性病灶列為適應症，而該共識每一條建議都沒有標註強度與等級；它指出低風險難證明的原因是這些人死於甲狀腺癌的機率不到 1%、殘存或復發只有 2% 到 3%，回溯性研究很難在這種底數上看出好處；它還有一句專給微小癌——一公分以下、沒有其他高風險特徵的乳突微小癌不該做，而這句只適用一公分以下，不能往上套到一到四公分。圖的最後是一個紅框的界線區塊，標題是「這張圖不會把四個試驗串成一串」，內容五條：上下兩塊回答的是兩個不同的問題，把四個串成「這四個都證明放射碘可以少做」是錯的；1.1 與 3.7 GBq 在這張圖上只是那兩個試驗的識別特徵，不是任何人的處方，你這一次用多少、怎麼準備、要不要住進去，依你醫院核子醫學科的規定；ESTIMABL2 的「低風險」永遠帶著它的排除條件，你報告上的「低風險」如果不是這一格，那個結論就不是為你做的；存活這一題沒有任何一個隨機試驗是以總存活當主要終點做的（IoN 的複合終點含死於甲狀腺癌，那不是總存活），把兩個試驗 1,280 人合併分析，無復發存活的風險比 0.96（0.80 到 1.15）、全因死亡 1.28（0.48 到 3.41），區間都寬到橫跨 1，這只能說「看不出差別」，不能說「一樣安全」；2017 年歐美的兩個核醫學會與兩個甲狀腺學會合組了跨學會工作小組來處理放射碘的爭議，2020 年他們的進度報告寫著可得的證據不足以提供任何確定的指引、他們無法達成共識——四個學會談都談不攏，兩個醫師給你兩種說法，是正常的。
en_alt: Schematic drawing four randomised radioiodine trials as two separate blocks, divided by a dashed rule labelled "Between the two questions: no arrow", because they answer two different questions. The first block is headed "Question one: whether to give radioiodine at all" and holds ESTIMABL2 and IoN. Its note says both are non-inferiority trials with the margin agreed in advance at five percentage points, and that a non-inferiority trial cannot show that something does not work - what it can say is "not worse". The ESTIMABL2 (France) card: randomised to radioiodine or none, 776 patients, all after total thyroidectomy. The event-free rate at three years was 95.6% with no radioiodine against 95.9% with it; at five years, with 698 patients evaluable, 93.2% against 94.8%. Both time points fall within the non-inferiority margin. The card notes that an "event" here is a composite - abnormal imaging or ultrasound, or a rise in thyroglobulin or antibodies - and is not recurrence and certainly not survival. Inside that card sits a second, red-bordered box headed "Who it excluded: this belongs in the same sentence as its conclusion", listing three exclusions: solitary papillary microcarcinoma of 1 cm or under, excluded outright, the trial's own stated reason being that ablation is not necessary in these patients; all node-positive disease; and pT2 and above. The box closes by recording what was enrolled - multifocal disease totalling one to two centimetres, or a solitary tumour of one to two centimetres, node-negative or not assessed - and states that the "low risk" this trial tested is not the low risk printed on a reader's report. The IoN (United Kingdom) card: also randomised to radioiodine or none, 33 centres, 504 patients, median follow-up 6.8 and 6.6 years. The crude recurrence-free rates at five years were 97.9% (96.1 to 99.7) with no radioiodine against 96.3% (93.9 to 98.7) with it, and the trial separately estimates a five-year absolute risk difference of 0.5 percentage points (95% confidence interval minus 2.2 to 3.2). The card states that the 0.5 is not those two rates subtracted: it is a separately estimated quantity, signed as the excess risk carried by leaving ablation out, and non-inferiority is declared because the top of that interval, 3.2, sits under the 5-point margin fixed in advance; subtract the two rates and you get 1.6 points, pointing the other way; and how the 0.5 was estimated cannot be said here, because the paper's methods section was not obtainable. Non-inferiority was met here too. Its endpoint differs from ESTIMABL2's: local recurrence or residual structural disease, distant metastasis and death from thyroid cancer counted together, with only 17 recurrences in the whole trial. The paper says it is still in follow-up, and the authors' conclusion is narrower than the entry criteria: pT1, pT2, node-negative or not assessed, with no adverse features. The lower half of that card is a small table headed "Inside the trial, the higher-risk patients really were at higher risk": of 46 patients with pT3 disease 4 recurred (9%); of 458 with pT1 or pT2, 13 (3%); of 47 with positive central nodes, 6 recurred (13%); and of 457 node-negative or not assessed, 11 (2%). The card closes by noting that the paper's next sentence is that these rates were similar in the patients who had no radioiodine, and that with only 17 events in the entire trial a subgroup in which no difference can be seen is not a subgroup in which there is none - this is "cannot be seen", not "shown not to exist". The second block is headed "Question two: how much to give" and holds HiLo and ESTIMABL1. Its note says every patient in these two trials received radioiodine, that what was randomised was the activity and the preparation, and that they say nothing whatever about whether to give it. The HiLo (United Kingdom) card: every patient received radioiodine, with a low activity of 1.1 and a higher activity of 3.7 GBq - the identifying feature of these two trials and nobody's prescription. The primary endpoint, the remnant cleared at six to nine months after treatment, was met in 85.0% on the low activity against 88.9% on the high activity; at a median follow-up of 6.5 years the cumulative recurrence at seven years was 5.9% against 7.3%, hazard ratio 1.10 (95% confidence interval 0.47 to 2.59). The card notes that the primary endpoint is a surrogate, not recurrence and not survival, and closes by saying that how much you yourself receive follows the rules of your hospital's nuclear medicine department. The ESTIMABL1 (France) card: again every patient received radioiodine, with the low activity of 1.1 randomised against the higher activity of 3.7 GBq together with the preparation, and again the primary endpoint was whether the remnant was cleared six to nine months after treatment. It closes by saying that using these trials to answer "whether" is running the two questions together. Below both blocks comes the point of the figure: inside one guideline, the strengths run in a counter-intuitive order. The introduction records that the 2025 edition divides recurrence risk into four tiers each carrying a probability - low, under 10%; low-intermediate, 10 to 15%; intermediate-high, 16 to 30%; and high, over 30% - and that those four percentages are probabilities of structural or biochemical recurrence, not mortality and not stage. Four rows follow, each giving the tier, the recommendation, the strength and the certainty. Low, under 10%: do not give routinely, strong recommendation, high certainty - this row is drawn with a heavy border. Low-intermediate, 10 to 15%, and intermediate-high, 16 to 30%: may be considered, conditional recommendation, low certainty. High, over 30%: give routinely, strong recommendation, moderate certainty. Distant metastases present at diagnosis: give, strong recommendation, moderate certainty. A yellow banner reads: set out in order it is plain, the hardest evidence is the evidence for not giving it. It adds that the guideline explains its own weakness in the middle tiers - too few studies look at those two tiers on their own - and that a systematic review lays it out further though it counts a different set of people - the middle box of the older three-tier stratification - with 11 observational studies seeing a benefit and 13 not, its authors adding that only a few of them had properly stratified populations, the boundaries having been redrawn since so that middle is not today's two middle boxes, while the shape of the disagreement has not changed. A further block records the European consensus: the 2022 European Thyroid Association consensus likewise lists high risk and known structural disease as indications, and not one of its recommendations carries a strength or a grade; it gives the reason low risk is hard to prove, namely that these patients have under a 1% chance of dying of thyroid cancer and only a 2% to 3% chance of persistence or recurrence, so a retrospective study can hardly demonstrate a benefit against a base rate like that; and it adds one line specifically about microcarcinoma, that papillary microcarcinoma of 1 cm or under with no other high-risk features should not be ablated, a line that applies to 1 cm and under and cannot be carried upward to tumours of one to four centimetres. The figure ends with a red-bordered block headed "This figure will not string the four trials together", holding five statements. The two blocks answer two different questions, so folding all four into "these four show radioiodine can be cut back" is wrong. The 1.1 and 3.7 GBq on this figure are the identifying feature of those two trials and nobody's prescription, and how much you receive, how you are prepared and whether you are admitted all follow the rules of your hospital's nuclear medicine department. ESTIMABL2's "low risk" always travels with its exclusions, and if the "low risk" on your report is not that cell then that conclusion was not made for you. On survival, no randomised trial has been run with overall survival as its primary endpoint (IoN's composite endpoint counts death from thyroid cancer, which is not overall survival): pooling the two trials, 1,280 patients in all, gives a hazard ratio for recurrence-free survival of 0.96 (0.80 to 1.15) and all-cause death 1.28 (0.48 to 3.41), intervals wide enough to straddle 1, which says "no difference is visible" and not "equally safe". And in 2017 the two nuclear medicine societies and the two thyroid associations, European and American, set up an intersocietal working group on the radioiodine controversy whose 2020 progress report states that the available evidence was insufficient to provide any definitive guidance and that they could not arrive at a consensus - if four societies cannot agree, two doctors giving you two answers is normal.
