不能整筆算在抑制頭上。第三組是心血管死亡。一，524 名分化型甲狀腺癌對 1,572 名同地區配對對照（世代：分化型甲狀腺癌病人）：校正後心血管死亡風險比 3.35（95% 信賴區間 1.66 到 6.74）；病人組內訊號的幾何平均值每下降十倍，校正風險比 3.08（1.32 到 7.21）。二，705,307 名吃甲狀腺素的美國退伍軍人（世代：服用甲狀腺素者，中位年齡 67 歲、88.7% 為男性，絕大多數不是甲狀腺癌）：訊號被壓下去的那一端心血管死亡校正風險比 1.39（95% 信賴區間 1.32 到 1.47）；吃太少、訊號高到不正常的那一端是 2.67（2.55 到 2.80）——兩端都有代價，而且吃太少那一端更大。第四段是同一群人身上好處和代價擺在一起：771 名低風險與中風險（當年的三級分層）的分化型甲狀腺癌病人，全部做全切，中位追蹤 6.5 年；結構性復發 43 人（5.6%）、術後骨質疏鬆 29 人（3.9%，只算女性）、術後心房顫動 17 人（2.3%）；依中位訊號分成壓與不壓兩組，復發風險完全一樣，風險比 1.02（信賴區間 0.54 到 1.91）；心房顫動與骨質疏鬆合起來算是 2.1（1.001 到 4.3）；女性術後骨質疏鬆 3.5（1.2 到 10.2）。結語寫：在這一格的人身上，多壓的那一點沒換到東西，代價倒是量得出來。第五段是半切的人為什麼也常常要吃藥：115 名做治療性單葉切除、沒做放射碘的低風險分化型甲狀腺癌病人裡，97 人（84%）術後訊號高過那篇研究採用的界線，其中 66 人（68%）開始吃左旋甲狀腺素、中位在術後 74 天，77% 至少調整過一次劑量；那個年代用的還是舊版那個偏低的目標，所以「要不要吃」這句話，問的其實是「你的目標訂在哪」。圖的最後是一個紅框的界線區塊，標題是「這張圖上不會出現一個可以拿去對號入座的數字」，內容五條：2025 年版把那組數值刪掉了，理由寫在表的註腳裡，把舊版的數字畫回這張圖上等於把一份已經被取代的寫法重新發出去，所以這裡一個都不畫；反方向的話也不成立，抑制治療只有一個隨機試驗而且是非劣性設計、結果落在界限之內，所以「已經證明沒用」這句話同樣沒有依據；代價那一側的數字大部分不是從甲狀腺癌病人身上算出來的，每一個都留著它的世代標籤；最常出事的地方不是吃太多，是自己不舒服就停掉或減半、然後好幾個月沒回診，吃太少那一端的代價在那筆 705,307 人的資料裡比吃太多還大，不舒服就回來講、不要自己調；最後是回診要問出口的四句——我現在的治療反應被分在哪一類、這個分類會不會改？你替我訂的目標是正常範圍內還是壓到正常以下？為什麼是這一邊？如果是壓到正常以下，我們打算壓多久？什麼時候會重新評估？如果我覺得心悸或睡不好，是該減量，還是先抽血？
en_alt: Schematic on how much of the lifelong tablet to take, whose most important feature is that no numeric TSH target appears anywhere on it. That absence is deliberate and is the subject of the figure, not an omission. The first part draws what the 2025 American Thyroid Association table actually gives now: four cells of words. Four rows read - excellent response, keep the signal within the normal reference range; indeterminate response, keep the signal within the normal reference range; biochemical incomplete response, below the normal reference range; structural incomplete response, below the normal reference range. The note explains that what these four cells hang on is not the recurrence-risk tier assigned at the time of surgery but the response-to-therapy category, which is only given after a period of follow-up and which changes. Beneath them the footnote to that table is quoted verbatim: "Data on optimal TSH target range are inconclusive and/or conflicting" - the data on the best target range are themselves inconclusive and they conflict with one another - and the recommendation it belongs to is a conditional recommendation with low certainty. The figure then says that this does not sound like an answer but is honest: the number your doctor gives you is no longer copied out of a guideline, it is a judgement made for you. The guideline adds a further line, that the benefits and harms of suppression and the target itself should be re-evaluated over time, which the guideline lists as good practice and does not grade. To the right of that panel on the desktop layout, and below it on the mobile one, sits a hatched box struck through with a cross, headed "This panel is empty, and deliberately so". Its text explains that the set of numbers a reader can look up and match themselves against belongs to the 2015 edition of the guidelines; that the 2025 edition deleted that set outright, leaving only the four cells of words above with no number to copy; and that this figure therefore does not draw them back in, because drawing them back in would mean reissuing a form of words that has already been superseded. A further block records that the new edition also says something the old one did not, quoted verbatim: "Long-term TSH suppression is not suggested for patients with low- or intermediate-risk disease who have no evidence of biochemical or structural recurrence", a conditional recommendation with low certainty. It then states plainly that this sentence uses the old three-tier language of low and intermediate risk while the recurrence-risk stratification in the same guideline has moved to four tiers, that the guideline does not explain how the two map onto each other, and that the figure does not translate it across either. The second part is the benefit side, in three cards. The first is the only randomised trial, from 2010 at a single Japanese centre, whose cohort was papillary carcinoma classified by the AMES system of the day, with most patients having had neither total thyroidectomy nor radioiodine: 218 patients in the suppressed arm against 215 not suppressed, disease-free survival as the endpoint, no difference between the arms, and a 95% confidence interval for the recurrence hazard ratio of 0.85 to 1.27. The card notes that it is a non-inferiority trial whose result fell inside the margin, so it cannot be written up as "suppression has been shown not to work"; a non-inferiority trial cannot demonstrate absence of effect, and all it can say is that in these patients not suppressing was not worse. The second card is a 2002 observational meta-analysis favouring suppression, whose cohort is studies from 1934 to 2001 covering 4,174 patients with papillary or follicular carcinoma of whom 2,880 were suppressed: the relative risk of disease progression, recurrence and death combined was 0.73 (confidence interval 0.60 to 0.88), although the period spanned is so long that neither surgery nor radioiodine was standardised across it. The third card is a 2024 observational meta-analysis restricted to adults with intermediate- and high-risk differentiated thyroid cancer and followed for five years: the composite of progression-free or disease-free survival gives a hazard ratio of 0.75 (95% confidence interval 0.48 to 1.17) and disease-specific and overall survival 0.69 (0.31 to 1.52), neither significant, while cardiac or skeletal adverse events are 1.82 (1.30 to 2.55) and significantly higher in the suppressed group. The third part is the cost side, arranged in three groups, with the first line of every card giving its cohort, because most of these figures were not calculated from patients with thyroid cancer. The bone density and fracture group holds three cards. First, 179 women on long-term thyroid hormone after thyroidectomy - cohort: women on long-term treatment after surgery for thyroid carcinoma, median age 59, 178 of them postmenopausal - in whom radiological vertebral fracture ran at 44.6% in the most suppressed group, 24.0% in the middle group and 4.3% in the least suppressed group; those three groups are the study's own division by measured signal rather than anybody's target, and within the most suppressed group women with normal bone density did not fracture any less. Second, 13 prospective cohorts and 70,298 participants - cohort: individual participant data from the general population, not patients with thyroid cancer - giving a hip fracture hazard ratio of 1.36 (95% confidence interval 1.13 to 1.64) with subclinical hyperthyroidism, and in the lowest signal band a hip fracture ratio of 1.61 (1.21 to 2.15, 47 events among 510) and a clinical vertebral fracture ratio of 3.57 (1.88 to 6.78), the last of which rests on 8 events among 162 people. Third, US veterans, 10,370 against 10,370 matched controls - cohort: patients with thyroid cancer, predominantly men - with osteoporosis at 7.3% against 5.3%, an odds ratio of 1.33 (95% confidence interval 1.18 to 1.49), but an odds ratio for signal and fracture of 1.01 (0.96 to 1.07), fractures being no more frequent: losing bone density and actually breaking something are not the same event. The atrial fibrillation group holds two cards. First, 2,007 community-dwelling people over 60 followed for ten years - cohort: community-dwelling older people, not patients with thyroid cancer, and their low signal was not caused by a tablet - in whom the lowest signal band had a ten-year cumulative incidence of 28% against 11% in those with a normal signal, an adjusted relative risk of 3.1 (95% confidence interval 1.7 to 5.5), with no difference at all in the mildly low band. Second, Korean national data of 113,791 patients with differentiated thyroid cancer against 455,188 matched controls - cohort: patients with differentiated thyroid cancer, the comparison being having the disease against not having it rather than suppression against no suppression - giving a hazard ratio for new atrial fibrillation of 2.07 (95% confidence interval 1.98 to 2.17), while patients in the same paper who had a lobectomy only reached 1.93 (1.72 to 2.15), so that the 2.07 cannot be charged in full to suppression. The cardiovascular mortality group holds two cards. First, 524 patients with differentiated thyroid cancer against 1,572 matched regional controls - cohort: patients with differentiated thyroid cancer - with an adjusted hazard ratio for cardiovascular death of 3.35 (95% confidence interval 1.66 to 6.74), and within the patients themselves 3.08 (1.32 to 7.21) per tenfold fall in the geometric mean of the signal. Second, 705,307 US veterans taking thyroid hormone - cohort: people taking thyroid hormone, median age 67 and 88.7% male, the great majority without thyroid cancer - in whom the suppressed end carries an adjusted hazard ratio for cardiovascular death of 1.39 (95% confidence interval 1.32 to 1.47) while the under-treated end, where the signal is abnormally high, carries 2.67 (2.55 to 2.80); both ends carry a cost and the under-treated end carries the larger one. The fourth part puts both sides in the same people: 771 patients with low- and intermediate-risk differentiated thyroid cancer under the three-tier system of the day, all after total thyroidectomy, median follow-up 6.5 years, with structural recurrence in 43 (5.6%), postoperative osteoporosis in 29 (3.9%, women only) and postoperative atrial fibrillation in 17 (2.3%). Split at the median signal into suppressed and not, the risk of recurrence was identical at a hazard ratio of 1.02 (confidence interval 0.54 to 1.91), atrial fibrillation and osteoporosis counted together gave 2.1 (1.001 to 4.3), and postoperative osteoporosis in women 3.5 (1.2 to 10.2). In this group of patients the extra suppression bought nothing, while the cost was measurable. The fifth part explains why people who had only half the gland removed so often end up on the tablet anyway: among 115 patients with low-risk differentiated thyroid cancer who had a therapeutic lobectomy and no radioiodine, 97 (84%) finished above the threshold that study used, of whom 66 (68%) started levothyroxine at a median of 74 days after surgery and 77% had the dose adjusted at least once; the target in use at the time was the low one from the old edition, so "do I have to take it" is really the question of where the target has been set, with the two proportions behind it set out in "Half the gland, or all of it". The figure closes with a red-bordered block headed "No number you can hold against yourself appears on this figure", holding five statements. The 2025 edition deleted that set of values for the reason written into the footnote of the table, and drawing the old edition's numbers back onto this figure would be reissuing a superseded form of words, so not one of them is drawn. The opposite claim does not hold either, because suppression has exactly one randomised trial, it is a non-inferiority trial and its result fell inside the margin, so "it has been shown not to work" has nothing behind it. Most of the cost-side figures were not calculated from patients with thyroid cancer, and each keeps its cohort label. The thing that most often goes wrong is not taking too much but stopping or halving the dose when feeling unwell and then not returning for months, the cost at the under-treated end of that series of 705,307 people being larger than the cost at the over-treated end. And finally four sentences for the next appointment: which response-to-therapy category am I in now and can it change; is the target within the normal range or below it, and why that side; if below, how long do we plan to keep it there and when will it be reviewed; and if I feel palpitations or cannot sleep, should I cut the dose or have a blood test first.

1，而且影像陰性；表上四個反應分類全部存在，這一欄的資料最多，指引整理的結構性復發率就是以這一欄的族群為準。右上格是全甲狀腺切除但沒做放射碘：同一格的線變成小於 2.5 ng/mL，差了十倍以上，不是筆誤；理由是放射碘會把手術留下的正常甲狀腺組織清掉，沒做的人那些組織還在，正常組織一樣會製造這個蛋白，底數本來就高；這一欄的結構性復發率整體比左上那一欄低。左下格是單葉切除、沒做放射碘：「反應良好」那一格根本不看甲狀腺球蛋白，看的是對側那一葉有沒有結節、有的話切片是不是良性、影像上有沒有異常淋巴結；而「反應不明確」與「生化性反應不完全」兩格在指引自己的表上直接寫 N／A，圖上照樣畫成兩個打叉、標著 N／A 的格子，不替它們補數字；指引對單葉切除後例行驗甲狀腺球蛋白的說法是不建議常規做，有條件建議、極低確定性，追蹤主力是超音波，不是那管血。右下格是單葉切除加放射碘：這一格在表上不存在，因為指引把判讀拆成三欄，所以圖上畫成一個打叉的空格，並寫明這張圖不替它生一條線出來。第二段解釋為什麼單葉切除那一欄不是同一種東西：2022 年那篇系統性回顧把三種情境分開報，單葉切除之後是 4 篇、561 人，全切但未做放射碘是 5 篇、751 人，全切之後做放射碘之前是 28 篇、7,618 人；它對第一種情境的逐字結論是「Following partial thyroidectomy, Tg measurement was not accurate for diagnosing recurrence or metastasis, or estimates were imprecise」，而且它給所有情境的證據品質評級都是 very low。紅框那一格寫 30 ng/mL 那個切點沒有被採用：2016 年確實有人提過單葉切除後用 30 ng/mL 當界線，那是 507 人的單中心世代、全部沒做放射碘，但 2025 年版沒有採用這個切點。旁邊一格寫就算在左邊那兩欄，第一次驗出來也不是定案：一個 299 人的世代（全部全切加殘存消融、之後沒再接受其他治療）裡，六個月到達谷底的只有 58%，十二個月 75%。第三段是四個反應分類與各自的結構性復發率，族群是成人分化型甲狀腺癌、全切加放射碘，也就是四宮格左上那一格的人，畫成五條範圍帶：反應良好 1–4%，其中一開始就被分在低風險的人是 0.2–2%；反應不明確 5% 到 15–20%；生化性反應不完全 20–53%；結構性反應不完全那一格畫成斜線，標「影像看得到」，因為它的定義是影像上看得到局部或遠端轉移而不是一個百分比。說明寫：全切但沒做放射碘那一欄的對應數字整體比較低，而這四格是「現在走到哪裡」，不是「一開始被分到哪裡」。接著兩格示範這套分類會改寫一開始的分組：588 人、中位追蹤 7 年的世代，一開始低風險 3%、中風險 21%、高風險 68% 出現持續性結構疾病或復發，前兩年達到反應良好之後重新分類，三格變成 2%、2%、14%；506 人、中位追蹤 10 年的世代是低 13%、中 36%、高 68%，達到反應良好者降到 1.4%。底下註記這兩組數字和分期那一篇裡那組（1.5%、5.4%、25%）不一樣，因為終點定義與世代都不同，同一格風險在不同研究裡會給出不同的百分比，這本身就是為什麼一開始那一格不是判決。第四段是抗體陽性的那兩成：大約兩成的分化型甲狀腺癌病人血中驗得到抗甲狀腺球蛋白抗體，而這不是「干擾」，是另一種追蹤模式。現行的免疫計量法在抗體存在時傾向低估，所以問題不是打折、是數字漂亮可能是假的；質譜法則敏感度不足；指引同一段寫得更白，沒有哪一套甲狀腺球蛋白檢驗在抗體存在時是完全準確的。引文框裡是指引的逐字句「Imaging is the primary modality for monitoring in this population」，有條件建議、低確定性。抗體本身則變成指標：用同一套試劑連續看趨勢，穩定或下降歸在反應不明確，上升歸在生化性反應不完全；所以在這兩成裡的人，超音波會排得比較密，而不是那管血抽得比較勤；每次驗甲狀腺球蛋白都要同時定量抗體，這一條指引列為良好實務，沒有給證據等級。第五段是那個停止點，畫成一條三站的時間軸：初次治療完成後六到十二個月做一次頸部超音波，之後的時間與頻率看復發風險和治療反應，這一條是良好實務、沒有給證據等級；五到八年，低風險、做過全切加放射碘、而且持續維持反應良好的人可以停掉常規的頸部超音波，之後每一到兩年驗生化指標就好，有條件建議、低確定性；十到十五年，持續反應良好的人不需要再繼續常規的生化監測，而且應該被視為已經達到完全緩解，這一條是良好實務、沒有給證據等級。旁邊寫兩個前提要一起記——低風險，而且持續反應良好；另一格寫單葉切除那一群人的資料更有限，指引的寫法是初次超音波陰性的話，之後每一到三年做一次、做五到八年。時間軸下方一行綠底的話：「完全緩解」這四個字，是這份指引第一次寫進條文裡，這也是 ATA 甲狀腺指引史上第一次寫出可以停。再下面兩格：為什麼現在不必再停藥或打針刺激才驗——一篇納入 10 篇、1,796 人的統合分析算出，在服用甲狀腺素的狀態下高敏感甲狀腺球蛋白測不到時，排除結構性疾病的陰性預測值是 99.4%（95% 信賴區間 98.9 到 99.9）；以及超音波怎麼排、什麼時候不必扎——短徑小於 8 到 10 毫米的可疑淋巴結可以先追蹤，除非它長大或威脅到喉返神經、氣管、食道、大血管，有條件建議、低確定性；而且指引給了反面的話，低風險而且反應良好的人做超音波並沒有因此找出有臨床意義的疾病，反而會因為偽陽性增加介入次數。圖的最後是一個紅框的界線區塊，標題是「這張圖不會替你把三欄合成一欄」，內容四條：四宮格裡的每一條線只屬於它自己那一格，把別人的數字拿來對自己的是門診裡最常拆的誤會；單葉切除那一欄的兩個 N／A 是指引自己寫的，不是這張圖沒查到，那兩格沒有線，所以那兩格不能用那管血下結論；第四格（單葉切除加放射碘）在表上不存在，因為指引把判讀拆成三欄；「可以停」有兩個前提，低風險而且持續反應良好，停的是癌症的例行監測，不是「以後都不用看醫師」，甲狀腺素的劑量要怎麼調是另一件事，2025 年版全文查不到一條規定多久驗一次促甲狀腺素的條文，這張圖也不替它補。最後一格是三句門診提問：我這種手術範圍、這種放射碘狀態，Tg 應該對哪一條線；我的抗甲狀腺球蛋白抗體是陽性還是陰性，如果是陽性我的追蹤要怎麼改；如果我這次還不符合停止監測的條件，請幫我寫下還差哪一項、大概還要幾年。
en_alt: Schematic drawing the reading of thyroglobulin as a four-cell map: across, whether radioiodine was given; down, how much of the gland was removed, total thyroidectomy or lobectomy. Top left is total thyroidectomy with radioiodine: the line for an excellent response is a nonstimulated thyroglobulin - the one drawn while you are taking your tablet - below 0.2 ng/mL, or a stimulated thyroglobulin below 1, with negative imaging. All four response categories exist in this column, the data are fullest here, and the structural recurrence bands the guideline collects come from this column's population. Top right is total thyroidectomy without radioiodine: the same cell's line becomes below 2.5 ng/mL, a difference of more than tenfold and not a typographical error, because radioiodine clears the normal thyroid tissue the operation left behind, that tissue is still present when radioiodine was not given, normal tissue makes this protein too, and the baseline is simply higher; the structural recurrence figures for this column are lower overall than for the cell on its left. Bottom left is lobectomy without radioiodine: the excellent-response cell does not look at thyroglobulin at all, but at whether the contralateral lobe has a nodule, whether a biopsy of it was benign, and whether imaging shows abnormal nodes. The indeterminate response and biochemical incomplete response cells are written N/A in the guideline's own table, and the figure draws them as two hatched, crossed-out cells labelled N/A rather than supplying a number. On routine thyroglobulin after lobectomy the guideline says it is not recommended routinely, a conditional recommendation with very low certainty, and ultrasound carries the follow-up rather than the blood test. Bottom right is lobectomy with radioiodine: this cell does not exist in the table, because the guideline splits the reading into three columns, so it is drawn as a crossed-out empty box stating that the figure invents no line for it. The second part explains why the lobectomy column is not the same kind of thing. The 2022 systematic review reports the three situations separately: after lobectomy, 4 studies and 561 patients; total thyroidectomy without radioiodine, 5 studies and 751 patients; after total thyroidectomy and before radioiodine, 28 studies and 7,618 patients. Its verbatim conclusion on the first situation is quoted - "Following partial thyroidectomy, Tg measurement was not accurate for diagnosing recurrence or metastasis, or estimates were imprecise" - and it rates the quality of evidence as very low in every situation. A red-bordered cell records that the 30 ng/mL cutoff was not adopted: it was indeed proposed for lobectomy in 2016, in a single-centre cohort of 507 patients, none of whom had radioiodine, but the 2025 edition did not take it up. Beside it, a cell records that even in the two left-hand columns the first result is not the verdict: in a cohort of 299 patients, all of whom had total thyroidectomy and remnant ablation and nothing further, only 58% had reached their nadir by six months and 75% by twelve. The third part sets out the four response categories with their structural recurrence rates, in adults with differentiated thyroid cancer after total thyroidectomy and radioiodine - the people in the top left cell - as five range bands: excellent response 1 to 4%, and 0.2 to 2% for those who were low risk from the start; indeterminate response 5% to 15-20%; biochemical incomplete response 20 to 53%; and structural incomplete response drawn as a hatched band labelled "visible on imaging", because it is defined by local or distant metastases on imaging rather than by a percentage. The note records that the corresponding figures in the column without radioiodine are lower overall, and that these four cells describe where a patient is now rather than where they were placed at the start. Two cells then show the classification rewriting the starting category: in a cohort of 588 patients with median follow-up 7 years, persistent structural disease or recurrence ran at 3% in those initially low risk, 21% at intermediate risk and 68% at high risk, and after re-classification at an excellent response in the first two years the three became 2%, 2% and 14%; in a cohort of 506 patients with median follow-up 10 years the figures were 13%, 36% and 68%, falling to 1.4% in those reaching an excellent response. A note records that neither set matches the figures in the sister article on staging, 1.5%, 5.4% and 25%, because the endpoint definitions and the cohorts differ, and that the same category giving different percentages in different studies is itself why the starting category is not a verdict. The fourth part is the one in five with antibodies: about one in five patients with differentiated thyroid cancer have detectable anti-thyroglobulin antibodies, and this is not interference but a different mode of monitoring. Current immunometric assays tend to underestimate when antibodies are present, so the problem is not that the number needs discounting but that a reassuring number may be false; mass spectrometry is not sensitive enough; and the same passage says plainly that no thyroglobulin assay is entirely accurate when antibodies are present. A quotation box carries the guideline's verbatim sentence, "Imaging is the primary modality for monitoring in this population", a conditional recommendation with low certainty. The antibody itself then becomes the marker: followed as a trend on one assay, stable or falling counts as an indeterminate response and rising counts as a biochemical incomplete response. So for that one in five the ultrasounds are booked closer together rather than the blood drawn more often, and antibodies must be quantified every time thyroglobulin is measured, which the guideline lists as good practice and does not grade. The fifth part is the stopping point, drawn as a timeline of three stations. At six to twelve months after initial treatment, one neck ultrasound, with the timing and frequency thereafter following recurrence risk and response to therapy, listed as good practice and not graded. At five to eight years, patients at low risk who had total thyroidectomy and radioiodine and have sustained an excellent response may stop routine neck ultrasound and move to biochemical testing every one to two years, a conditional recommendation with low certainty. At ten to fifteen years, patients with a sustained excellent response need no further routine biochemical monitoring and should be regarded as having reached complete remission, listed as good practice and not graded. Beside the timeline, two conditions that travel together - low risk, and a sustained excellent response - and a note that the data are thinner for patients who had a lobectomy, for whom the guideline's wording is that if the first ultrasound is negative, one every one to three years, for five to eight years. A green band below the timeline records that "complete remission" is written into the recommendations here for the first time, and that this is the first time an ATA thyroid guideline has written down a stop. Two further cells follow: why stimulation is no longer needed before the test, from a meta-analysis of 10 studies and 1,796 patients in which undetectable high-sensitivity thyroglobulin on levothyroxine gave a negative predictive value of 99.4% (95% confidence interval 98.9 to 99.9) for excluding structural disease; and how the ultrasounds are spaced, where a suspicious node under 8 to 10 mm in short axis may be followed rather than sampled unless it grows or threatens the recurrent laryngeal nerve, trachea, oesophagus or great vessels, a conditional recommendation with low certainty, and where the guideline says the opposite of the instinct that more scans mean more safety - in patients at low risk with an excellent response, ultrasound did not find clinically meaningful disease and increased interventions through false positives. The figure ends with a red-bordered block headed "This figure will not merge the three columns into one", holding four statements: every line in the four cells belongs to its own cell alone, and reading your own report against somebody else's number is the commonest misunderstanding there is to undo in clinic; the two N/A cells in the lobectomy column are the guideline's own rather than something this figure failed to find, and cells with no line cannot be concluded from the blood test; the fourth cell, lobectomy with radioiodine, does not exist in the table because the guideline splits the reading into three columns; and "you can stop" has two conditions, low risk and a sustained excellent response, with what stops being routine cancer surveillance rather than seeing a doctor, the levothyroxine dose a separate matter, no recommendation on how often TSH should be checked findable anywhere in the 2025 text, and none supplied here in its place. A closing cell carries three sentences to say out loud with the follow-up schedule in front of you: with my extent of surgery and my radioiodine status, which line should my Tg be read against; are my anti-thyroglobulin antibodies positive or negative and, if positive, how does my follow-up change; and if I do not yet qualify to stop surveillance, please write down which condition is missing and roughly how many years are left.

是亞洲人，那只是族裔組成、不是「特別適合誰」。四張卡下面一格寫四個試驗不是頭對頭比較：指引逐字承認從來沒有隨機試驗直接比較過第一線那兩個藥，它的取捨是沒有可對應標靶的進展性病人用這兩個藥之一、多數情況 lenvatinib 是首選（強烈建議、高確定性），cabozantinib 用在曾用過上述藥物並惡化的人（強烈建議、高確定性）——這是順序，不是排名。再一格寫再分化：國際甲狀腺腫瘤學組 2025 年的聲明寫碘攝取恢復的比例在各試驗之間是33% 到 95%、腫瘤反應率 11% 到 80%，而試驗之間在納入條件、用藥時間、放射碘活度、劑量計量上差異很大，最關鍵的一句是「Randomised studies are missing」；唯一完成的第三期問的還不是救援——ASTRA 收術後高風險、未依基因篩選的病人，233 人隨機，十八個月完全緩解率 40% 對 38%，勝算比 1.07（95% 信賴區間 0.61 到 1.87），陰性。右欄最後一格寫台灣那一段不在這張圖上：有沒有藥證、健保有沒有收載、給付規定有沒有寫這個癌別與條件是三件事，答案不一樣，混著講必定出錯；這張圖不寫哪一支藥在台灣給付於哪一種甲狀腺癌，逐字條文在〈在台灣，這條路怎麼走〉那一篇。兩欄之間是一條垂直的虛線，圖上沒有任何箭頭把左欄的判準連到右欄的某一支藥。圖的最後是一個紅框的界線區塊，標題是「這張圖不會替你把四個試驗排成一張排行榜」，內容四條：四格用同一把尺畫是為了看見每一格自己的兩根柱子差多少，不是為了比較哪一支藥的柱子比較長，族群、線數、對照組都不同；每一個信賴區間都標了層級，99%、96%、95% 的區間不能放在同一句話裡比寬窄；這些藥買到的是把病灶壓住的時間，不是治癒；會不會讓人活得比較久，上面四個試驗沒有一個是為了回答這一題設計的——總存活在四個裡面都只是次要或探索性終點，而且四個都讓安慰劑組在惡化後換吃真藥，交叉本身就會把這個終點弄糊；逐一是 sorafenib 沒有做出顯著差異（0.80，0.54 到 1.19）、cabozantinib 的 0.76（0.45 到 1.31）同樣不顯著、dabrafenib 加 trametinib 的期中分析未達顯著（0.66，0.36 到 1.19）而那個試驗還在進行、lenvatinib 根本沒有發表過總存活的風險比或檢定；沒有一個證明了總存活的好處，那和「總存活沒有好處」不是同一句，第二句這張圖不寫；再分化沒有隨機證據，唯一完成的第三期是陰性的，而且它問的還不是救援。最後一格是三句門診提問：我被判定放射碘無效是根據哪一條判準；我的病灶現在有在長嗎、比上次長了多少；如果吃了三個月沒有把病灶壓住，我們的下一步是什麼。
en_alt: Schematic in two columns: on the left the criteria for radioiodine-refractory disease, on the right four phase III trials with their numbers of patients, median progression-free survival and hazard ratios. A grey band across the top states that nothing in the left column carries an evidence grade: the two gates are listed by the guideline as good practice, which it does not grade, the criteria themselves sit in the discussion paragraph beneath them and carry no recommendation strength at all, and the guideline says these criteria will go on changing. The first cell on the left holds the two gates, tagged "good practice, which the guideline does not grade": first, a patient who has never had ablative or therapeutic radioiodine cannot be diagnosed as refractory to it, and those who qualify should have it first because that is how the answer is found; second, a patient already judged refractory should not be given empiric radioiodine again, and other treatments are to be considered. The second cell holds the two strong criteria: a lesion visible on imaging or PET with no iodine uptake on the post-therapy scan; or progression within six months of one appropriately dosed radioiodine treatment where the post-therapy scan did show uptake. The third holds the two supportive criteria: no uptake on the diagnostic scan while the lesion is visible on imaging, which predicts a poorer response though some such patients still have a positive post-therapy scan; and uptake in only some lesions, which does not rule radioiodine out but is not enough on its own. A further cell records that refractory does not mean a short time left: the guideline says in the same section that some patients die within three to five years and that others survive a long time with stable or extremely slowly progressive disease, so the first step after "refractory" is often not a drug at all - patients who are asymptomatic, stable or barely progressing, or who carry significant comorbidity, may be imaged every three to twelve months on suppressive thyroid hormone therapy, a conditional recommendation with low certainty. A yellow cell states that the threshold for starting a drug is imaging and not a blood test: the guideline requires visible progression of lesions on imaging before systemic therapy, not a blood curve climbing upwards; a rising thyroglobulin on its own is written down as not constituting a reason to start; and the trials below enrolled people with progression on imaging in the first place. The left column closes with the recommendation to test tumour tissue for biomarkers before systemic therapy starts, strong with moderate certainty, noting that the drugs chosen by genotype work well but rest on very few patients, whose numbers are in the article while this figure carries only the phase III trials. The right column opens with a red cell warning that not every confidence interval is 95%: the hazard ratio 0.21 for lenvatinib is a 99% confidence interval; the response rate in the cabozantinib interim analysis is a 99% confidence interval; the progression-free survival hazard ratio 0.22 for cabozantinib is a 96% confidence interval; and only the hazard ratios in the sorafenib and BRAF phase III trials are 95%. A note adds that when the levels differ the widths of the intervals cannot be read in the same sentence, and that "median progression-free survival not reached" for cabozantinib is the older wording from the interim analysis, the 2022 extended analysis being the one to use. Four trial cards follow, each drawing two bars on the same scale in months, drug above and control below. The lenvatinib phase III enrolled 392 patients with radioiodine-refractory, progressive differentiated thyroid cancer, 261 on drug and 131 on placebo, with median progression-free survival 18.3 months against 3.6 months and a hazard ratio of 0.21 (0.14 to 0.31) tagged as a 99% confidence interval; response was 64.8%, 4 of them complete, against 1.5%, and on overall survival this trial published no overall-survival hazard ratio or test at all, only that median overall survival had not been reached in either arm; discontinuation for adverse events was 14.2% against 2.3%, of 20 deaths during treatment 6 were judged drug-related, and hypertension, diarrhoea, fatigue, loss of appetite and weight loss each exceeded four in ten. The sorafenib phase III enrolled 417 patients, 207 on drug and 210 on placebo, with median progression-free survival 10.8 months against 5.8 and a hazard ratio of 0.59 (0.45 to 0.76) at 95%; overall survival showed no significant difference, hazard ratio 0.80 (0.54 to 1.19), while 71.4% of the placebo arm crossed over to the drug after progressing and the authors write that the overall-survival result may be confounded by it; response was 12.2% (24/196), all partial; dose interruption 66.2%, reduction 64.3%, discontinuation for adverse events 18.8%, and serious adverse events 37.2% against 26.3%. The cabozantinib phase III is given from its 2022 extended analysis: 258 randomised, median follow-up 10.1 months, median progression-free survival 11.0 months against 1.9, hazard ratio 0.22 (0.15 to 0.32) tagged as a 96% confidence interval, with the interval around the median of 11.0 months also 96%, from 7.4 to 13.8; response was 11.0% (95% confidence interval 6.9 to 16.9) against 0, grade 3 or 4 adverse events 62% against 28%, and the overall-survival hazard ratio of 0.76 (0.45 to 1.31) is likewise not significant, the authors writing that crossover will confound future analyses of overall survival; in the interim analysis of 187 patients the response rate was 10/67 among the first 100 randomised (15%, 99% confidence interval 5.8 to 29.3) against 0/33 and did not meet the prespecified threshold for significance. The BRAF phase III read out after the guideline was written: 153 previously treated patients with BRAF V600E-positive, radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer, randomised 101 to 52, median progression-free survival 12.8 months against 3.7, stratified hazard ratio 0.38 (0.25 to 0.57) at 95%, with the interval around the median of 12.8 months 10.2 to 21.2 at 95%; response was 57% against 4%; the interim analysis of overall survival has not reached significance, stratified hazard ratio 0.66 (0.36 to 1.19), and that trial is still running; the authors conclude for second-line use and 86% of those enrolled were Asian, which is the ethnic composition of the trial and not a statement about who the drug suits. Below the four cards, a cell records that these are not head-to-head comparisons: the guideline admits in so many words that no randomised trial has ever compared the two first-line drugs directly, its judgement being that a progressing patient with no matched target should have one of the two and that in most cases lenvatinib is preferred, a strong recommendation with high certainty, while cabozantinib is for patients who have progressed on one of those drugs, also strong with high certainty - a sequence and not a ranking. A further cell covers redifferentiation: the 2025 International Thyroid Oncology Group statement reports restoration of iodine uptake ranging from 33% to 95% between trials and tumour response from 11% to 80%, with wide differences in eligibility, timing, radioiodine activity and dosimetry, and the sentence that matters most is "Randomised studies are missing"; the only completed phase III was not asking about salvage at all, ASTRA having enrolled high-risk postoperative patients who were not genomically selected, randomised 233 of them and found complete remission at eighteen months in 40% against 38%, odds ratio 1.07 (95% confidence interval 0.61 to 1.87), a negative result. The right column closes by stating that the Taiwan part is not on this figure: whether a drug is licensed, whether it is listed by the National Health Insurance, and whether the reimbursement rules name this cancer and these conditions are three separate questions with three different answers, and running them together goes wrong every time; this figure does not say which drug is reimbursed in Taiwan for which thyroid cancer, and the rules are transcribed verbatim in the sister article, "How this goes in Taiwan". A vertical dashed rule separates the two columns and no arrow anywhere on the figure joins a criterion on the left to a drug on the right. The figure ends with a red-bordered block headed "This figure will not turn four trials into a league table", holding four statements: the four cells are drawn on one scale so that the gap between the two bars within each cell can be seen, not so that one drug's bar can be compared with another's, because the populations, the lines of therapy and the control arms all differ; every confidence interval is printed with its level, and intervals at 99%, 96% and 95% cannot have their widths compared in the same sentence; what these drugs buy is time with the disease held down rather than a cure, and on whether they make people live longer not one of the four trials above was designed to answer that question - overall survival is a secondary or exploratory endpoint in all four and all four let the placebo arm cross over after progressing, which by itself blurs the endpoint; one at a time, sorafenib showed no significant difference (0.80, 0.54 to 1.19), cabozantinib's 0.76 (0.45 to 1.31) is likewise not significant, the interim analysis of dabrafenib plus trametinib did not reach significance (0.66, 0.36 to 1.19) and that trial is still running, and lenvatinib published no overall-survival hazard ratio or test at all, so that none of them proved a benefit in overall survival, which is not the same sentence as "there is no benefit in overall survival"; and redifferentiation has no randomised evidence, the one completed phase III was negative, and it was not even asking about salvage. A closing cell carries three sentences to ask before a drug is started: on which criterion was I judged refractory to radioiodine; are my lesions growing now and by how much since last time; and if three months of this does not hold the disease down, what is our next step.

年那份共識的話不掛在美國那本名下。左欄標題是髓質癌，時間以年計，長自夾在濾泡之間的濾泡旁 C 細胞，分泌的是降鈣素和癌胚抗原（CEA）。第一格「一句話換三個結論」：放射碘對髓質癌沒有用，因為 C 細胞不抓碘；把促甲狀腺素壓低也沒意義，它不聽那個訊號長大，術後吃藥只是補回身體需要的量；追蹤抽的不是甲狀腺球蛋白，是降鈣素和 CEA。第二格是紅底的：開刀之前先排除嗜鉻細胞瘤，並引美國甲狀腺學會 2015 年髓質癌指引的原句「a PHEO should be excluded prior to thyroidectomy」；說明寫嗜鉻細胞瘤長在腎上腺、會陣發地釋放讓血壓飆高的荷爾蒙，它若還在，麻醉和手術的刺激可能把血壓推到危險的高度，所以髓質癌確診後常常不會馬上排刀，那幾管血、那張腹部影像不是多做的，是把順序排對。接著是它為什麼會跟髓質癌一起出現：MEN2A 是髓質癌加上嗜鉻細胞瘤、或原發性副甲狀腺機能亢進、或兩者都有；MEN2B 發病更早、更具侵襲性，幾乎每個帶因者都會有髓質癌。遺傳那一段把兩種突變分成兩張卡：胚系 RET 會傳——大約四分之三的髓質癌是偶發的、四分之一是遺傳性，後者幾乎都來自 RET 的胚系突變，體染色體顯性、外顯率接近完全，「胚系」是指全身細胞都帶著它、抽血驗得到，也才有傳下去的問題；腫瘤裡的體細胞 RET 不會傳——偶發型髓質癌裡大約一半，不同綜述寫 50%，或 50% 到 80%，腫瘤細胞裡驗得到 RET 突變，那是只存在於那顆瘤的體細胞突變，不會傳給小孩。黃底一句：「一半的髓質癌帶 RET 突變」和「一半的髓質癌是遺傳的」，是兩句不同的話。遺傳諮詢那一格引原句「Genetic counseling and genetic testing for RET germline mutations 66.7%，低惡性度 1.0%。黃底一格寫一本十一年沒有改版的指引：髓質癌目前能引的還是 2015 年那本，六十七條建議，用的是從美國預防服務工作小組那套改寫的 A 到 F 分級；十一年不是小事，這期間多了兩個選擇性 RET 抑制劑、一個頭對頭的第三期試驗，所以你會遇到「指引沒寫、醫師在談」，那通常不是醫師亂來，是書還沒改。左欄最後是台灣端：民國 112 年的癌症登記報告裡髓質癌男性 19 rapidly enlarging thyroid mass should be considered a medical emergency and managed accordingly.」，用 should，代表全體一致同意。接著一格說明這份共識把用字和票數綁在一起：should 是全體一致同意，is recommended 是至少七成同意，may be considered 是同意度不到七成、或要看當地有什麼資源；另一本是美國甲狀腺學會 2021 年的未分化癌指引，三十一條建議加十六條良好實務聲明，用美國內科醫師學會那套評分法，兩本年份與評分法都不同，這張圖分開標名字。氣道那一段先寫一篇 17 人個案系列的引言記載未分化癌有超過三成的個案「可能以」急性呼吸道阻塞表現，並標明那是背景泛稱、不是那 17 17.6%，那個數字來自一家醫院連續兩年的 17 位病人，中位總存活 11 個月、一年存活 36%；作者另外寫，不要在病房或急診室以局部麻醉嘗試，應在手術室由有經驗的頭頸外科醫師執行。灰底一句收尾：兩邊放一起就是這段的實際形狀——不建議常規先做，但也不能等到窒息那一刻才第一次談，這個討論要在清醒、能講話、家屬在場的時候做完。接著是那管血多快送出去，引原句「Rapid BRAF V600E testing should be performed as soon as possible after diagnosis (ideally within 24 hours) when targeted therapies are available and timely testing is feasible.」，那是同一份共識第六條建議、同樣是 93%），換句話說約有六成的腫瘤沒有這個突變，兩個數字不衝突，一個是統合的合併值、一個是那家中心的臨床現實；技術上做得到，有一組用細針抽吸檢體做數位聚合酶連鎖反應，兩位病人的結果都在二十四小時內出來，那是兩個人的個案報告、不是常規。存活那一段畫成兩張並排的卡：左邊標「歷史數字」，寫中位存活四個月，並註明原文寫 historically、意思是歷史上如此，這是過去的數字；右邊標「近年世代」，寫中位總存活 9.5 個月，並註明那是一家大型醫學中心 2000 到 2019 年 479 位未分化癌病人的資料，全世代中位總存活 0.79 年、也就是 9.5 個月。下面一格分年代看一年與兩年存活：2000 到 2013 年那 227 人是 35% 和 18%，2017 到 2019 年那 152 人是 59% 和 offered——被提供、被說明，這張圖不會叫你去要求任何家人接受檢測，指引寫的是醫師對病人本人的告知義務、不是替你聯絡誰；哪一支藥在台灣給付於哪一種甲狀腺癌兩欄都不寫，逐字條文在〈在台灣，這條路怎麼走〉那一篇。最後一格是兩欄各一句的門診提問：髓質癌——開刀前，嗜鉻細胞瘤那一項驗過了嗎、結果是什麼；未分化癌——BRAF V600E 送了沒有、哪一天送的、大概哪一天會回。
en_alt: Schematic setting two different diseases side by side in two columns: medullary carcinoma on the left, anaplastic carcinoma on the right, separated by a dashed rule with no arrow of any kind between them. A grey band across the top states that three histologies mean three books, three years and three grading systems: the American Thyroid Association guideline that can still be cited for medullary carcinoma is the 2015 one, for anaplastic carcinoma it is the 2021 one, and the differentiated guideline was revised in 2025; this figure keeps the two guidelines separately named, and the sentences from the 2026 Latin American Thyroid Society consensus are not attributed to the American book. The left column is headed medullary carcinoma, where the clock runs in years, arising from the parafollicular C cells that lie between the follicles and secreting calcitonin and carcinoembryonic antigen. Its first cell, "one sentence, three consequences", says that radioiodine does nothing here because C cells do not take up iodine; that suppressing TSH is pointless because this disease does not grow to that signal, the tablet after surgery only replacing what the body needs; and that follow-up measures calcitonin and CEA rather than thyroglobulin. A red cell states that phaeochromocytoma must be excluded before the operation, quoting the 2015 American Thyroid Association guideline on medullary thyroid carcinoma verbatim: "a PHEO should be excluded prior to thyroidectomy". The explanation is that phaeochromocytoma sits in the adrenal gland and releases in bursts hormones that drive the blood pressure up, that the stimulus of anaesthesia and surgery can push the pressure to dangerous heights if it is still there, and that this is why an operation is often not booked the moment medullary carcinoma is diagnosed - the blood tests and the abdominal scan are not extras but the order things have to be done in. Next, why it turns up alongside medullary carcinoma: MEN2A is medullary carcinoma together with phaeochromocytoma, or with primary hyperparathyroidism, or with both; MEN2B is earlier in onset and more aggressive, and almost every carrier develops medullary carcinoma. The genetics are split into two cards. Germline RET can be passed on: about three quarters of medullary carcinomas are sporadic and one quarter hereditary, the hereditary ones nearly all arising from a germline RET mutation, autosomal dominant, with penetrance close to complete, and germline meaning every cell in the body carries it, that a blood test can find it, and that the question of passing it on exists at all. Somatic RET inside the tumour cannot be passed on: in roughly half of sporadic medullary carcinomas - different reviews write 50%, or 50% to 80% - a RET mutation is found in the tumour cells, a somatic mutation present only in that tumour and not passed to children. A yellow line adds that "half of medullary carcinomas carry a RET mutation" and "half of medullary carcinomas are hereditary" are two different sentences. The counselling cell quotes the guideline verbatim - "Genetic counseling and genetic testing for RET germline mutations should be offered to" - and notes that the same document also says patients with presumed sporadic disease should have testing for a germline RET mutation, because looking sporadic is not the same as being sporadic. What the counselling asks is set out: who in the family had what and at what age, particularly thyroid, adrenal and parathyroid; whether anyone had episodic high blood pressure, palpitations or sweating; whether anyone had thyroid surgery very young; and whether you have children or plan to. The guideline also lists pre-implantation or prenatal diagnostic testing, in those words, as an option to be discussed. The next cell quotes "The duty to warn a competent and capacitated patient" and explains that what is written is the doctor's duty to inform the patient, that the direction is that things are explained clearly to you rather than anyone being contacted on your behalf, that whether, when and whom to tell is yours to decide, and that this figure tells nobody to be tested. A further cell sets down plainly who carries the consequence of not testing, listing the three tiers by the position of the RET mutation: highest risk M918T, high risk codon 634, and other pathogenic variants moderate. For the high-risk tier the guideline sentence reads "Children in the ATA-H category should have a thyroidectomy performed at age 5 years or earlier"; for the moderate tier it is physical examination, neck ultrasound and calcitonin from the age of five; and for the highest tier it is earlier still, the guideline's own sentence being unobtainable so that a review is cited second-hand for surgery within the first year of life. The cell states that this is set down so that the reader knows what is behind that door, not as an instruction to knock on anybody's. The doubling time follows: what predicts is not one high reading but the doubling time. A French database followed 65 patients whose calcitonin was still abnormal after total thyroidectomy with bilateral neck dissection, drawn as three cards - doubling time under 6 months, 12 patients, 3 alive at five years (25%) and 1 at ten years (8%); 6 months to 2 years, 11/12 (92%) at five years and 3/8 (37%) at ten; longer than 2 years, 41 patients, all still alive at the end of the study. The note records that only doubling time was an independent predictor on multivariable analysis, that TNM stage and the EORTC score were significant on univariable analysis and stopped being significant once they entered the multivariable model, and that the figure has a boundary, being drawn from patients left with biochemical disease after surgery and not applicable to someone whose calcitonin became undetectable straight after the operation. A meta-analysis of ten studies adds that CEA doubling time predicts better than calcitonin, so both are measured, which is why nobody says "it has gone up" on the strength of one blood test. A further cell ties this to the pathological grade: calcitonin doubling time is 8.51 plus or minus 3.22 months in high grade against 38.42 plus or minus 11.19 months in low grade, and 66.7% of high-grade patients have a doubling time under one year against 1.0% of low-grade patients. A yellow cell records a guideline unrevised for eleven years: the citable guideline for medullary carcinoma is still the 2015 one, sixty-seven recommendations graded A to F on a system adapted from the US Preventive Services Task Force; eleven years is not nothing, since two selective RET inhibitors and one head-to-head phase III trial have arrived in the meantime, so a reader will meet "the guideline does not say this, but the doctors are discussing it", which is usually not the doctor going off-piste but the book not having been rewritten. The left column closes with Taiwan: in the national cancer registry report for 2023, medullary carcinoma accounted for 19 men and 29 women, 48 cases in all, 1.26% of male and 0.64% of female thyroid malignancies that year; survival data for medullary carcinoma in Taiwan and the hereditary share return no entry; and which drug is reimbursed in Taiwan for which thyroid cancer is not on this figure, the rules being transcribed verbatim in the sister article, "How this goes in Taiwan". The right column is headed anaplastic carcinoma, where the clock runs in weeks: other sections are about months and years, and this column is about this week. A red quotation carries recommendation 1 of the 2026 Latin American Thyroid Society expert panel consensus verbatim - "A rapidly enlarging thyroid mass should be considered a medical emergency and managed accordingly." - with "should" meaning unanimous agreement. The next cell explains that this consensus ties its wording to its votes: "should" is unanimous agreement, "is recommended" at least seventy per cent, and "may be considered" under seventy per cent or dependent on local resources. The other book is the 2021 American Thyroid Association guideline on anaplastic carcinoma, thirty-one recommendations plus sixteen good practice statements on the American College of Physicians grading system; the years and the grading systems differ, so the figure names them separately. The airway section states first that the introduction of a 17-patient case series records that more than three in ten cases of anaplastic thyroid cancer "may present" with acute airway obstruction, marking that as a background generalisation rather than a rate calculated from those 17 people, and that this is why "should a tracheostomy be done first" is usually raised in the first days after diagnosis. It then quotes "Elective tracheostomy should not be routinely performed." and labels it as recommendation 23 of the 2026 Latin American Thyroid Society consensus, with "should" and unanimous agreement. The next cell says plainly that the 2021 American Thyroid Association guideline does not carry this as a recommendation - a full-text index was searched and none of the phrasings hit; it discusses tracheostomy among the elements of a decision, saying it relieves upper airway obstruction immediately but requires a great deal of care education, and it does carry a separate recommendation that the vocal cords be assessed at every patient's first visit - so "do not do an elective tracheostomy" is not attributed to the American book here, being the Latin American consensus speaking. The reasoning cell records that tracheostomy markedly reduces quality of life, does little to lengthen survival, and that bleeding and tumour growing out through the stoma are both common complications, which is why thinking has changed over the past decade, while the same passage writes the other half too: what may have to be done if acute respiratory distress occurs must be discussed in advance. A figure cell gives emergency tracheostomy for symptomatic airway obstruction a 30-day mortality of 17.6%, from 17 consecutive patients at one hospital over two years with median overall survival 11 months and one-year survival 36%, the authors adding that it should not be attempted under local anaesthesia on the ward or in the emergency department but in theatre by an experienced head and neck surgeon. A grey line closes the section: put the two halves together and that is its real shape - not routinely done in advance, and not first discussed at the moment of suffocation, the conversation having to be finished while the patient is awake, able to speak, and with family present. The BRAF section quotes recommendation 6 of the same consensus verbatim - "Rapid BRAF V600E testing should be performed as soon as possible after diagnosis (ideally within 24 hours) when targeted therapies are available and timely testing is feasible." - again "should" and unanimous. Why the hurry: because the result changes what is done that week; the pooled prevalence of BRAF V600E in anaplastic carcinoma is 33%, with individual studies ranging from 0% to 93%, so about six in ten tumours do not carry it, and the two figures do not conflict, one being a pooled value and the other the clinical reality of one centre. It is technically possible: one group ran digital polymerase chain reaction on fine-needle aspirate and had results back within twenty-four hours for two patients, a case report of two people rather than routine practice. Survival is drawn as two cards side by side. The left is labelled historical and reads "median survival four months", with a note that the source writes "historically", meaning that this is how it used to be and that it is a figure from the past. The right is labelled recent cohort and reads "median overall survival 9.5 months", with a note that the study writing that sentence is itself data on 479 patients with anaplastic carcinoma at one large medical centre between 2000 and 2019, whose median overall survival across the whole cohort was 0.79 years, that is 9.5 months. Below, the same cohort is read by era for one- and two-year survival: the 227 patients from 2000 to 2013 reached 35% and 18%, and the 152 patients from 2017 to 2019 reached 59% and 42%, with a hazard ratio between the eras of 0.50 (95% confidence interval 0.38 to 0.67), and a note that this is one hospital's figure and not a world average. A further cell places two more beside them: 97 patients at another academic hospital between 2000 and 2021, median overall survival 6.5 months (confidence interval 4.3 to 10.0), and a Spanish and Portuguese registry of 214 patients at 4.5 months; the differences coming from the era, from whether that hospital can complete molecular testing and start treatment within days, and from the extent of disease at diagnosis, anaplastic carcinoma always being stage IV with only the letter A, B or C varying. The right column closes with Taiwan: in the national cancer registry report for 2023, anaplastic carcinoma accounted for 22 men and 30 women, 52 cases in all, and survival and treatment data for anaplastic carcinoma in Taiwan return no entry in the official statistics. The figure ends with a red-bordered block headed "This figure will not mix the two columns, and it tells nobody to be tested", holding four statements: these are two columns because they are two diseases, the calcitonin and doubling time on the left cannot be carried across and the clock that runs in weeks on the right cannot be carried back, and no arrow joins them; "Elective tracheostomy should not be routinely performed" is recommendation 23 of the 2026 Latin American Thyroid Society consensus while the 2021 American Thyroid Association guideline does not carry it as a recommendation, and this figure keeps the names apart; the genetics cell describes what counselling asks and the word the guideline uses, which is "offered", so the figure does not tell anyone to ask a relative to be tested, what the guideline writes being the doctor's duty to inform the patient rather than to make contact on their behalf; and which drug is reimbursed in Taiwan for which thyroid cancer appears in neither column, the rules being transcribed verbatim in the sister article, "How this goes in Taiwan". A closing cell carries one sentence from each column to be said out loud first: for medullary carcinoma, before surgery, has the phaeochromocytoma question been tested for and what was the result; and for anaplastic carcinoma, has BRAF V600E been sent, on what day, and roughly when does it come back.
